cards.name: basic-3d-scene
cards.summary: An impress.js-style spatial presentation: cards are scattered through 3D space at different positions/rotations/scales, the camera takes the inverse of each step's pose and flies to align with them in turn, and the final step pulls out to an OVERVIEW
cards.use_when: Spatialised telling of a concept / roadmap / three-step method; a replacement for flat slides where "every step changes the spatial viewpoint"
cards.duration: about 7.5s (225f@30fps; four stops, three flights of 28/32/32f, each stop dwelling ≥30f)
cards.energy: Medium (each transition has a spatial surprise, the dwell sections are quiet for reading the cards)
cards.intent: Turn "turning the page" into "travelling through the space of ideas": each card has not only a position but also an attitude (at the second stop the world turns left by 38°, at the third the whole frame lies on its side by 90°), and when the camera aligns with it the audience's world turns too — the spatial change itself becomes the ceremony of "entering a new chapter".

styles.label: basic-3d-scene
styles.description: impress.js-style spatial presentation: cards scattered through 3D space at different positions/rotations/scales; the camera takes the inverse of each step's pose and flies to align with each in turn, with the final step pulling out to an OVERVIEW

cards.name: crash-zoom-punch
cards.summary: A wide shot rams to a target close-up in one beat (6f), with a choice of two landings — overshoot rebound (elasticity) or a crash stop with screen shake (weight)
cards.use_when: The "name-calling" shot in a feature section — pressing the audience's gaze onto a target card/module in a single beat; for emphasis-level moments use the crash stop
cards.duration: about 0.5s of action + holds before and after (action 6–11f, front hold ≥30f to establish the wide shot, back hold ≥45f to read the close-up)
cards.energy: High (an instantaneous impact, not sustained high energy)
cards.intent: A slow push-in (spotlight-hero-card) is "please look", a sudden push-in is "look at this!" — slamming within one beat from the wide shot to the close-up, leaving the gaze no choice. The landing finish comes in two flavours: the rebound is elasticity ("look at this"), the crash stop with screen shake is weight ("that's the one"), chosen by the level of emphasis.

styles.label: crash-zoom-punch
styles.description: A wide shot crash-zooms to the target close-up in one beat (6f), with a choice of landing: overshoot rebound (elasticity) or a hard stop with screen shake (weight)

cards.name: cursor-flyover
cards.summary: After a whole-page overhead view, the camera flies in turn to four feature areas for zoom-in close-ups, an SVG cursor arriving a step ahead to point, each click leaving a ripple and triggering a UI response, and finally pulling back to the overhead view
cards.use_when: A feature tour of a single-page product: one shot takes the audience through all four feature areas, the cursor acting as the "tour guide's finger"
cards.duration: about 8.0s (240f@30fps; overhead 22f · four stops of 44f each (flight 20f + dwell 24f) · pull-back 24f · hold 18f)
cards.energy: Medium (equal-pace cruising, with rhythm marked by click ripples)
cards.intent: A shot-saving alternative to "four features, four edited segments": one continuous camera strings the four corners into a single tour route, and the cursor is the audience's attention proxy — wherever it goes and clicks, the audience looks. Spatial continuity also lets the positional relationships between the features be remembered along the way.

styles.label: cursor-flyover
styles.description: After an overhead view of the whole page, the camera flies in turn to four feature areas with zoom-in close-ups; an SVG cursor arrives a beat ahead to point, clicks leave ripples and trigger UI responses, and finally the camera pulls back to the overhead view

cards.name: depth-layer-moves
cards.summary: Layered-depth camera move — a multi-layer parallax slider: 3 layers with a speed gradient traversing sideways to create depth, and the protagonist floating up as the slider settles
cards.use_when: Sections where a flat screenshot should "have thickness": a sideways tour of a card deck / list / whole page
cards.duration: 4–5.5s sustained (demo 165f)
cards.energy: Medium (finish-oriented)
cards.intent: Panning a whole page is "looking at the page", layered depth is "being inside the space of the page". The parallax slider adds depth to a sideways move (the principle of the Disney multiplane camera, the same finish as the Linear film).

styles.label: multiplane
styles.description: Layered depth camera move: a multi-layer parallax slider where 3 layers with a speed gradient slide sideways to create depth, and the hero lifts up as the slider settles

cards.name: graze-face-tour
cards.summary: A steeply tilted surface-hugging roaming close-up — the lens skims low across the UI surface (sidebar tree / top bar / list acting as terrain), page text initially hovers above the interface with a same-shape soft shadow, and as the camera advances it accelerates down and sticks back onto the interface one after another
cards.use_when: A tour of feature areas (flying over the UI as a landscape); paired with a dark stage + neon rim light for a product "inner world" section; interface content making its entrance area by area
cards.duration: single section 4–5s; multiple sections can relay to extend it
cards.energy: Medium-high (continuous camera advance + continuous element landing, high information density)
cards.intent: Shoot the UI as terrain: a steeply tilted close-up turns the sidebar tree, navigation and list rows into landforms sweeping past, with shallow depth of field reinforcing the "hugging the surface". The heart of the shot is **text sticking down from the air**: text/components do not fade in in place, but hover above the interface (raised on the 3D z axis), cast a same-shape soft shadow onto the interface while in the air, and as the camera advances they accelerate down and stick back one after another, the shadows converging and vanishing with height — the audience sees the interface "complete itself" as the camera passes. The shadow is the perceptible crux: without the shadow, the hovering reads as an ordinary displacement entrance; with the shadow, the spatial relationship holds instantly.

styles.label: graze-face-tour
styles.description: Steep-angle surface-hugging tour close-up: the camera flies low across the UI surface (sidebar tree / top bar / list as terrain), with page text initially hovering above the interface casting a matching soft shadow, then accelerating down onto the interface one after another as the camera advances

cards.name: overhead-camera-moves
cards.summary: Two overhead-shot reveals — tilt-reveal (the tilt straightens up to reveal) and overhead-tabletop-drop (a tabletop card array slides sideways then dives suddenly in)
cards.use_when: Openings/transitions that tell their story through the "pitch angle": use A for a single-page establishing shot, and B for touring multiple pages and picking one to dive into
cards.energy: A medium / B medium-high
cards.intent: The library's overhead viewpoint has always been a gap — crane-rise is a rise of "translation + scaling" (the pitch angle does not move), and space-camera pattern C drone-dive is a dive-and-landing in one continuous shot; these two patterns let **the pitch angle itself tell the story**: A is a reveal — the whole page lies flat via rotateX, and the opening shows only a glowing perspective narrow band along the far upper edge (like the first light on the skyline), the camera "looks up" and rights itself, and the content floods into view row by row, like lifting a drawing on a desk; B is a choice — three page cards lie flat as a tabletop card array, and the camera, shooting overhead, slides sideways past them in turn (Wes Anderson tabletop), then at the target page dives suddenly in and straightens up into a full screen, "looked around the whole lot, and this is the one". Choosing: use A for a single-page opening, B for a multi-page transition/opening.

styles.label: tilt-reveal
styles.description: Inside a perspective container the whole page lies flat at rotateX -80° and rises upright over ~43f, with rotateX/scale/translateY sharing out-cubic and a slight overshoot at the end
styles.use: Opening establishing shot; single subject

styles.label: overhead-tabletop-drop
styles.description: A card array lies flat at rotateX 62°; the pan segment moves only translateX, sliding sideways past, and the drop segment runs angle/scale/offset channels together to dive into the final composition
styles.use: Pick one after a multi-page tour; works as either a transition or an opening

cards.name: space-camera-moves
cards.summary: Two 3D-spatialised camera moves — exploded-view (components blow apart along Z and then reassemble) and drone-dive-landing (a drone dive and landing)
cards.use_when: Highlight sections that shoot a flat page as a 3D object; both patterns are "big moves", with a total of ≤2 uses per film
cards.duration: A 170f (5.7s, the whole run of blow-apart – hover – reassemble – closing title); C 105f (3.5s, dive 69f + settle hold 36f) one-way dive
cards.energy: High
cards.intent: The depth-layer card adds depth to a pan — the layers move, but the page is still a page. These two patterns go further: the whole page is treated as one 3D object, and the camera (or the world) performs live-action-grade manoeuvres around it. The narrative semantics of the two take one slot each: A says "let's see what it is made of" (a teardown display, the language of Apple launch films); C says "slam from an overview onto the protagonist" (a god's-eye view diving straight into a hero close-up, whole → focus).

styles.label: exploded-view
styles.description: After the whole page tilts in 3D, components explode out along the Z axis with stagger and hover, then after a beat reassemble in reverse order with a screen shake to close
styles.use: Architecture/composition display: 'what's in this product'; module overview segments

styles.label: drone-dive-landing
styles.description: Hover at a near-vertical high angle → plunge into a steep dive → air-cushion deceleration stopping on a hero card close-up
styles.use: Opening establishing shot → introducing the topic; chapter start where a global map slams into a single point

cards.name: steep-tilt-glide
cards.summary: With a fixed camera, an upright page stands sideways in 60° strong perspective (near at right, far at left), and the page itself slides along its own 3D lateral direction past the lens (the object moves, the camera does not), the slide carrying speed ghosting, text components hovering and sticking down, revealed from dark to bright
cards.use_when: A showpiece tour of long pages / multi-block UIs (content sliding in turn past a fixed camera position); a dark-stage neon tonality; the "side-sweep" camera position complementing the surface-hugging camera card
cards.duration: 4s (120f) single shot; the wider the page, the longer it can be stretched
cards.energy: Medium-high (perspective showmanship + continuous motion, but the rhythm is even)
cards.intent: Stand the page up as a slanted wall: the camera is pinned and does not move, 60° strong perspective puts the right edge in your face and lets the left edge vanish at the vanishing point, and the page slides laterally along its own plane — the content sweeping past in turn like the carriages of a train. The crux is **the object moves, the camera does not**: perspective/origin/rotY are constants throughout, and the only quantity that moves is the page's local translateX — once the camera moves, the semantics turn into camera-move showmanship, whereas the drama here is "the page showing itself off". The angle converged over three rounds to exactly 60° (-45° "not right" → -53° "a bit bigger" → -60° chosen).

styles.label: steep-tilt-glide
styles.description: With a fixed camera, an upright page stands sideways in 60° strong perspective (near on the right, far on the left), and the page itself slides along its own 3D horizontal axis past the camera (object moves, camera doesn't), the slide carrying velocity ghosting, text components hovering and then landing, and the page revealed from dark to light

cards.name: tension-camera-moves
cards.summary: Two emotional camera moves — bullet-time freeze-orbit and pull-back isolation, where the camera "feels" on the audience's behalf rather than "looks"
cards.use_when: The camera language for emotional nodes (awe / closing); complementary to the "showpiece big moves" of space-camera-moves — these two patterns are small in action and heavy in emotion
cards.duration: 5–6s (150–170f) per pattern; ≤2 patterns in the whole film (≤1 use of each)
cards.energy: A high / B low closing
cards.intent: The three patterns of space-camera-moves are highlight showpieces of "shooting the page as a 3D object"; these two are the opposite — the action itself is restrained, and all the force lies in the emotional semantics: A says "this moment is worth stopping time to look at" (moving elements are frozen, and the camera orbits to scrutinise); B says "in the end only this one thing remains" (while pulling back the surroundings go out layer by layer, a lone point suspended to close the whole film). Each pattern takes one emotional slot, and they are the direct vocabulary at the storyboard stage for "what should the audience feel in this section".

styles.label: bullet-time-freeze-orbit — Freeze orbit
styles.description: A chart freezes entirely halfway through growing, the camera sweeps rotateY 55° around the suspended UI plane and back, then time resumes and the growth finishes
styles.use: Crowning moment for key data/charts; the one beat 'worth stopping the clock to look at'

styles.label: pull-back-isolation — Pull-back isolation
styles.description: Pulling back from a close-up of the glowing main card, sibling cards go dark with stagger by distance and the background sinks to black, leaving the lone card suspended at the center of the dark field
styles.use: Closing; the curtain call of 'the whole video exists for this one number'

cards.name: terminal-3d
cards.summary: Three terminal windows scattered through 3D space, the camera flying between them with a sine pull-back midway; at each window a command is typed out like a typewriter and results slide out line by line — a spatial narrative flow of command execution
cards.use_when: CLI/workflow demos for developer products: shooting "a three-step command" as a three-stop spatial journey
cards.duration: about 8.2s (246f@30fps; three stops each dwelling about 2–3s + two 30f flights)
cards.energy: Medium (the flights give motion, the typing gives rhythm, and the whole is a steady technical narrative; closing on a ● READY highlight)
cards.intent: Terminal output is by nature the anti-cinematic language of "flat scrolling", and this card spatialises it: each command occupies a physical window in space, and the camera visits the windows one by one as if walking through a machine room. The pull-back mid-flight lets the audience glimpse "there are more windows" — the sense of the full picture of the workflow.

styles.label: terminal-3d
styles.description: Three terminal windows scattered through 3D space, the camera flies between windows with a sine pull-back along the way, and at each window a typewriter taps out a command and results slide out line by line; a spatial narrative flow of command execution

cards.name: before-after-slider-scrub
cards.summary: Before/after comparison slider - "before / after processing" two versions overlaid, the divider bar first flung hard and then swept slowly, with the new version "developing" into view where the bar has passed
cards.use_when: Effect-comparison segments for AI enhancement / optimisation / refactoring features ("before vs after" explained in one shot)
cards.energy: Medium (the fast fling is the hit point, the slow sweep is the reading period)
cards.intent: The standard comparison grammar of AI image product launch films: the same frame "before processing" (low-contrast, murky) and "after processing" (the clear version) are overlaid, and a vertical divider bar with a round handle is first flung hard from the left end to 70% (with an overshoot rebound), pauses for a beat, and then sweeps back at about 1/5 of the speed so the viewer can see the difference clearly - **the speed contrast between the fast fling and slow sweep is the rhythm**: the fast fling announces "it changed", and the slow sweep proves "where it changed".

styles.label: before-after-slider-scrub
styles.description: Before/after comparison slider: 'before' and 'after' versions are stacked, and the divider handle first whips fast then sweeps slowly, with the new version 'developing' into view behind the handle

cards.name: chart-live-moves
cards.summary: Three styles of live charts - oscilloscope-stream (the curve is written in real time at the right end + a sudden spike), unit-dot-swarm-regroup (the dot swarm migrates in three acts and gathers into a number), axis-rescale-shock (a new value bursts out of the frame and forces the y axis to rescale)
cards.use_when: Data-narrative segments; respectively telling "real-time-ness", "every number is a person" and "growth does not fit"
cards.energy: Medium-high (the data is the plot)
cards.intent: A chart is not an illustration but a plot. The premise shared by the three styles (a measured precedent): **a real chart context is required** - real axis labels / real data / real copy; greyscale placeholder bars cannot test the expressive power of a data narrative. A oscilloscope-stream: the point where the curve is written is pinned at the right end and rises and falls, old data flows out of the frame to the left, and midway there is one sudden spike (amplitude 2.2×, the readout jumping large and turning the accent colour) - "real-time" need not be spoken, and there is also an event; B dot swarm regroup: 320 dots (each dot ≈40 renders) scatter → gather into three clusters (with real labels floating: Promo/Launch film/ Explainer) → line up into bars (real axis labels) → gather into a dot-matrix large number "12,847" - the same batch of dots, and the viewer can follow one particular dot and watch it fall back into line; C axis shock: the line climbs normally, and the new value breaks through the chart's ceiling guideline and bursts out 226px (an accent-colour thick line inserted into the title area, crashing into the upper-right KPI number), pauses for half a beat, and the y axis rescales with a "whoosh" (old ticks fly out / new ticks slide in / the grid densifies / the old line is flattened into the horizon), the new value drops back + a true-value label springs - using "the axis cannot hold it" to act out growth.

styles.label: oscilloscope-stream
styles.description: Sampling window pans 8px/f + cosine-envelope spikes + a braking stop to true stillness
styles.use: Monitoring / real-time products: a 'living' system

styles.label: unit-dot-swarm-regroup
styles.description: Three-act spring staggered migration (stiffness 150, stagger 8f), with the dot matrix forming a number in the final act
styles.use: User-count / composition narratives: 'every dot is a person'

styles.label: axis-rescale-shock
styles.description: Breaks out of the frame by 220px + a three-part linked rescale (ticks change / grid densifies / old line flattens) + 8px shake
styles.use: Growth-curve highlight: taking 'off the charts' literally

cards.name: gauge-readout-moves
cards.summary: Two styles of gauge readout - needle-sweep-selftest (the ignition self-test needle flung through the full arc and then dropping back to the true value) and tape-scroll-fixed-pointer (the pointer stays still while the scale tape scrolls past, plus a sprint and brake)
cards.use_when: Dashboard opening rituals / reveals of performance metrics; A for the power-on feel of multiple dials, B for a big jump in a single metric
cards.energy: Medium-high (mechanical ritual type)
cards.intent: Turn "reporting a number" into the body movement of an instrument: A is a car's ignition self-test - the three side-by-side dials in the card have their needles first "swish" through the full arc (270°), the ticks swept over light up in turn, and then the needles spring back and settle on the real values, with the multiple dials staggered into a wave, and on settling the value beneath each dial pops out on the same frame - the range lights up first, then the number is reported, a sense of oath-taking at the opening; B is airspeed-tape grammar - the readout window + pointer are pinned to the centre line of the frame, and a scale tape running the full height of the picture scrolls past behind the window as a whole, first creeping slowly against the old upper limit, then after the upgrade sprinting (peak ~100px/f), and at the end a spring brake with an overshooting swing back, "the world moves, the needle does not", and the size of the value becomes a displacement distance you can see.

styles.label: needle-sweep-selftest
styles.description: Needle outbound ~12f ease-out whipping to a full-arc sweep, return ~20f with a 5-8° overshoot swing-back settling on the true value; multiple gauges staggered 3-5f; the readout below the dial pops up on the same frame as settling
styles.use: Dashboard opening / system-ready ceremony

styles.label: tape-scroll-fixed-pointer
styles.description: Long tick-mark tape translate: slow-crawl segment → 45px/f sprint for ~25f → spring brake with overshoot swing-back to a stop; the readout in the window refreshes in sync
styles.use: A single large metric jump (performance doubled / quota raised)

cards.name: scroll-brake-moves
cards.summary: Two styles of hard-braking a long scroll - changelog-scroll-brake basic style (a high-speed long scroll with exponential deceleration stopping precisely in position + the target lifting) and brake-reticle-lock combined style (the reticle snapping shut on the same frame as the hard brake)
cards.use_when: Changelog / release history / long-list segments: "always shipping, and today's is the biggest"; use B when the stopping point needs a stronger sense of impact
cards.duration: A 4-5s / B 5s
cards.energy: High start, medium finish (speed-contrast type)
cards.intent: The Linear changelog video grammar: a whole year of update logs as a long scroll sweeping past at high speed (smeared into a colour band), brought to a precise hard stop by exponential deceleration on the entry for this release, which lifts off the surface and highlights while the rest dim down - the density tells "always shipping", and the hard stop tells "today's is the biggest". B is a combined variation: on the hard-brake frame, **on the same frame**, four L-shaped corner marks fly in from off-screen and snap onto the stopping-point entry - the "clunk" of the hard brake and the "click" of the snap resonate on a single frame (the crux of the combination: the corner marks' launch frame = the list's first stopped frame, and offsetting them degrades into two moves placed side by side).

styles.label: changelog-scroll-brake
styles.description: translateY sweeps ~2400px (out exp exponential deceleration over ~50f), with blur driven by the frame-to-frame displacement difference (0-6px, clearing automatically); the row at the stop point lifts with scale 1.03 + shadow + 3px outline, while the others fade to opacity 0.38
styles.use: Basic version of the changelog section

styles.label: brake-reticle-lock
styles.description: Scroll in three stages: sin-in acceleration → cubic-out hard deceleration overshooting by +30px → rebound settling; blur=v×0.12 capped at 24px; corner marks fly in from off-screen at ±620/±320 with Easing.back(2.4) and snap on, the highlight completes within 6f, and the label pops out with back(2.6)
styles.use: Highlight sections where the stop point needs a stronger sense of impact

cards.name: timeline-travel
cards.summary: Timeline traverse - the camera accelerates along a horizontal scale axis sweeping past the version ticks, a card springs up and holds briefly at each tick passed, and it brakes hard and pushes in at the last tick
cards.use_when: Changelog / milestone / history segments (another way of shooting "we are always shipping"); division of labour with scroll-brake-moves: that card is a vertical list hard-braking, this card is a horizontal journey through time
cards.energy: Medium-high (a rhythm-type shot of acceleration → hard brake)
cards.intent: Shoot the product's version history as a journey along a timeline (the title-sequence precedent of 反恐王国, literally "Counter-Terror Kingdom"): the camera makes a three-stage variable-speed horizontal traverse of slow start → sprint → hard brake, with the v1.0/v2.0/v3.0 ticks sweeping past in turn, and as each one is passed its card springs up from the tick line - history flashing by outside the window, with a hard stop on "today" and a push-in. The speed itself tells "development is fast", and the hard stop tells "now matters most".

styles.label: timeline-travel
styles.description: Timeline lateral travel: the camera accelerates along a horizontal scale axis past version ticks, each card popping upright and pausing briefly as it passes a tick, with a hard stop and push-in at the final tick

cards.name: assemble-then-type-flyin
cards.summary: On an empty dark grid, text-free component skeletons fly in from all directions and snap into place; then text flies in character by character, rotating in 3D space, headline first and small annotations last, and the page takes shape once everything has landed
cards.use_when: Openers where a page/poster "grows itself"; capability showcases for layout products; two-stage storytelling from skeleton to finished layout
cards.duration: about 5.6s (168f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium-high (sparse skeleton stage, dense text stage; energy rises monotonically to the close)
cards.intent: Split "page generation" into two clearly distinct stages: first set up the skeleton (frames, cards, dividers, colour blocks, all without text), then fill in the text. The text uses per-character 3D rotation because the skeleton stage only has flat translation: the two stages must differ in motion dimension, otherwise the viewer cannot read "this is the second step".

styles.label: assemble-then-type-flyin
styles.description: On an empty dark grid, text-free component skeletons fly in from all sides and snap into place; then the text flies in character by character, rotating through 3D space and landing in place, headline first, small labels after, until the page is complete

cards.name: aurora-bloom-bg-flip
cards.summary: A light grey background with purple-orange soft-focus blobs rising from the bottom, then the whole background is darkened to near-black within about 0.36s and the blobs are pressed down to an afterglow; the copy blurs out and blurs in with a sentence swap in sync, with a gap between sentences and no cross-fade
cards.use_when: Narrative turning points ("For years… → everything changed"); the beat in a brand film where it is pulled from set-up to accent; section switches between light and dark colour schemes
cards.duration: about 5.2s (156f@30fps)
cards.energy: Low to high (the first 2/3 is build-up, the instant of darkening is the accent of the whole film)
cards.intent: Use the "background inversion" as an accent mark: for the first 56% let the aurora rise slowly and let the viewer settle into the light background, then in under 0.4s press the whole frame to near-black — this reads more like a "page turn" than any zoom or white flash. The sentence swap must land after the inversion, with a gap in between, so that the viewer first takes in the change in the picture before reading the new sentence.

styles.label: aurora-bloom-bg-flip
styles.description: On a light gray background, soft-focus purple-orange blobs rise from the bottom; then within about 0.36s the whole background darkens to near-black and the blobs compress into an afterglow; copy swaps in sync with blur-out then blur-in, with a gap between phrases and no cross-fade

cards.name: brand-frame-snap
cards.summary: A brand-colour frame grammar: a thick solid-colour frame grows ahead of the content and wraps the full screen, and the screen-recording window drops into the frame; on a mode switch the whole frame hard-flips colour on the same frame and the in-window layout swaps on the same frame, so a single borderColor handles chapter navigation, status signalling and brand exposure at once
cards.use_when: The full-film wrapping layer for two-mode / two-chapter product films (blue = mode A, green = mode B colour coding); branded wrapping of real screen-recording footage
cards.duration: A single colour flip ~4.7s (140f); the frame itself can stay on screen for the whole film
cards.energy: Medium (high at the instant of the flip, a quiet wrapping layer the rest of the time)
cards.intent: A real screen recording laid straight across the full screen has no brand presence, and adding a logo watermark looks cheap. This card "mounts" the recording with a thick brand-colour frame: the frame **appears before the content** (set up the frame, then put in the picture, for a sense of ceremony), and from then on the frame colour becomes the semantic code of the whole film — in the demo cobalt blue = Design, orange-red = Dev Mode (blue/green in the original film; the key is opposing hues + a lightness difference). At a chapter switch the whole frame hard-flips colour within one frame, with no gradient; the hard colour cut is the visual equivalent of a "gear-shift" sound effect; the in-window layout goes A→B on the same frame, and the corner label and badge change text in sync, three things on the same frame resonating to hammer home the "mode switch". Division of labour with theme-switch-moves: that card changes the UI's own skin (with a sweeping boundary), whereas this card changes the "frame", the wrapping layer (same frame, no boundary); the semantics are mode/chapter switching, not theme switching.

styles.label: brand-frame-snap
styles.description: Brand-color frame grammar: a thick solid-color frame grows ahead of the content to enclose the full screen, and the screen-recording window drops inside it; on a mode switch the whole frame hard-flips color on the same frame as the in-window layout changes, so a single borderColor handles chapter navigation, status signaling and brand exposure

cards.name: fui-hud-moves
cards.summary: FUI/HUD reticle snap: reticle-lock-on, a viewfinder made of four L-shaped corner marks, flies in from off-screen, overshoots and rebounds, then snaps shut and locks onto the target
cards.use_when: Any "look here" call-out of a target (replaces drawing a red arrow or circle, with no frozen frame)
cards.duration: 2–3s (demo 90f)
cards.energy: Medium-high (the snap frame is the hit point)
cards.intent: A motif from sci-fi fictional interfaces (Jarvis/Territory) that can be neutralised: capture in motion. Four L-shaped corner marks rush in from off-screen, overshoot and rebound, snap onto the four corners of the target element with a "click", and pop a label — division of labour with freeze-annotate: that card freezes the frame to annotate, while this card calls out targets while the picture keeps flowing.

styles.label: reticle-lock-on
styles.description: FUI/HUD reticle lock: reticle-lock-on, a viewfinder made of four L-shaped corner marks flies in from off-screen, overshoots and rebounds, then snaps onto the target and locks
styles.use: Calling out a target; hitting a sound-effect downbeat

cards.name: glow-flyline-moves
cards.summary: Three dark-field light-spot and flyline variants: glow-orb-ambient as a light-spot noise floor, flyline-arc as a flyline connection, and orb-flyline-relay as a same-frame resonance combination
cards.use_when: Atmosphere and data storytelling for the single dark-field section of a film: use A to lay the noise floor, B to explain data flow direction, C when you want the background to answer the foreground; the Linear website feel
cards.energy: A low (noise-floor level) / B medium / C medium-high
cards.intent: This is the first card in the library that lives entirely on a **dark field**. The precedent of "a white background makes brightening invisible", read in reverse, is: to play with light, go to the dark field first. A is the breathing of space — three large light spots drift organically on a dark background, passing behind the central frosted-glass card, with their colour staining the card face through the glass, and the card edge glowing as the nearest light spot approaches, so the background is no longer dead; B is the verb of data — a glowing arc "fires" from card A to card B, with a bright dot head leading and a fading light tail, and the landing point outline pulsing to light up, so the link between metrics has a direction for the first time; C is the weld of A+B — on the frame the flyline lands, the neighbouring light spot surges brighter on the same frame, so the ambience layer and the event layer **resonate on the same frame**, answering each other rather than each performing alone (the crux of the combination: remove the shared resonance frame and it degrades into two cards side by side).

styles.label: glow-orb-ambient
styles.description: Three 500-700px radial light blobs + blur(100px) drifting on dual sine waves; card-edge glow is driven by the weighted max of blob distance [180,720]px→[1,0]
styles.use: Base layer for dark-field sections; card breathing feel

styles.label: flyline-arc
styles.description: Hand-written Bezier sampled at 100 segments, grown over 22f with out-cubic; a glowing head is conditionally mounted to lead, and segment opacity fades by distance from the head; the landing point gets an outline pulse and can hand off in relay
styles.use: Data flow direction / metric relationships; dashboard storytelling

styles.label: orb-flyline-relay
styles.description: A+B welded: the blob surge and card pulse share the landing frame, brightening by 1+1.6×surge, rising over 5f and dissipating over 15f
styles.use: Dark-field highlight sections; closing with a three-card relay

cards.name: icon-performance-moves
cards.summary: Icon performance: attention-bounce, an attention-seeking bounce (the icon jumps repeatedly with increasing height + squashes on landing + the camera is drawn to it)
cards.use_when: Half-screen icon close-up sections; introducing a new feature
cards.energy: Building up, an introduction
cards.intent: The first batch of the icon-animation category to enter the library: the icon is a performer the camera shoots up close, not a micro-interaction in a corner of the UI. attention-bounce is macOS Dock vocabulary — the video-shotcraft app icon in the Dock jumps 4 times in place, each higher than the last (0.35→1.2 times the icon height), squashing on every landing (final jump width 1.2x height 0.8x) + a ripple splash, neighbouring icons gradually lose focus, and on the highest jump the camera nudges 8% toward it (drawn to it); once settled it pops open the "New in Shotcraft" feature panel — cutting "user attention" into the narrative.

styles.label: attention-bounce
styles.description: Icon performance: attention-bounce, an attention-seeking bounce (the icon jumps in increasing height with squash on landing, and the camera is drawn to it)
styles.use: Introducing a new feature: 'look at me' → camera looks at it → it opens a panel

cards.name: impact-feedback
cards.summary: Two hit-feedback variants: hit-counter combo counting (hit-stop + damage numbers + combo count pop-ups), and anime-impact anime strike frames (negative + speed lines + chromatic dispersion)
cards.use_when: The "instant of the hit" when an element lands/collides — giving slams and sudden stops a game-grade feel; pick the variant by intensity tier
cards.duration: n/a (an element-level technique that piggybacks on the landing action; the frames each variant occupies are in the parameters table)
cards.energy: High (instantaneous impact)
cards.intent: When an element slams into place without an instant of "it hit", the landing reads as a PowerPoint fly-in. Game juice (Vlambeer's screenshake theory) and anime-direction impact frames give the same answer: for the few frames of the hit, bite down on time, and only then does the impulse reach the viewer's hands. The two variants form an intensity ladder: B uses a local hit-stop layered with damage numbers and combo count pop-ups to cut a feature list into a combo, with the strongest storytelling feel; C is the heaviest punch — three frames of negative flip and an exploding speed-line burst on a sudden stop, the highest emphasis level and the most stylised.

styles.label: hit-counter — Combo counter
styles.description: Three cards slam in one after another; each hit = 2f hit-stop + a damage number floating up + a ×N counter incrementing with escalating emphasis
styles.use: Rapid-fire feature-point segments, telling 'many features' through combos; strong gamification language

styles.label: anime-impact — Impact frames
styles.description: 3f of full-frame negative inversion + radial speed lines + red-cyan chromatic split on the crash-zoom hard stop, all removed on the 4th frame
styles.use: The single climactic punch of the whole video; the cap on emphasis level

cards.name: light-play-moves
cards.summary: Two light-effect variants: spotlight-sweep, a spotlight sweeping across text, and sheen, a single-point sweep of light
cards.use_when: Treating light as another kind of brush stroke (sweep/wipe): dark-field headline reveal (A), crowning a hero card (B)
cards.energy: A medium / B low
cards.intent: "Light" in the library had only ever had one spot-shot technique, spotlight-hero-card; these two variants make light into a system, with two kinds of brush stroke and two duties: A is the **sweep** — a headline almost invisible on a dark field is swept bright by a swinging cone of light, lighting up wherever the light goes; the difference from spotlight-hero-card is that that one lights a card, this one sweeps text; B is the **wipe** — a 45° highlight band wipes slowly across a dark-ink hero card once, clipped by its rounded corners, a silent coronation. Everything is on a dark background or a dark hero — **brightening is invisible on a white background** (precedent), and that is the foundation of this whole card.

styles.label: spotlight-sweep
styles.description: Two layers of the same text: the dark version stays at 0.07, the bright version follows the light spot via a radial mask, and after the cone of light swings back and forth twice it freezes fully lit
styles.use: Dark-field headline reveal opening

styles.label: sheen-sweep
styles.description: A 45° highlight band translateX sweeps once across a dark ink card, clipped by overflow hidden with rounded corners
styles.use: A single 'coronation' for the hero card during a still segment

cards.name: radial-ripple-phone-chips
cards.summary: Four layers of concentric circles on a warm sand background breathe out of phase like water ripples, the feed inside the central phone mockup's screen scrolls slowly on its own, and white chips on both sides spring-pop in one after the other and hover
cards.use_when: "This is it" freeze-frame shots for mobile products; introduction sections with feature points split across both sides; product panoramas for the opener/closer
cards.duration: about 5.6s (168f@30fps)
cards.energy: Low (quiet, with a sense of breathing; the continuous swell of the concentric circles keeps it from going dead)
cards.intent: Put the phone at the dead centre of the frame with the fewest moves and make it "alive": the concentric circles handle the atmospheric breathing, the auto-scroll inside the screen proves "there is content running in there", and the chips on both sides call out the feature names. Each of the three layers of motion is extremely slow, and only stacked together do they avoid looking still — this is the standard recipe for a product freeze-frame shot.

styles.label: radial-ripple-phone-chips
styles.description: On a warm sand background four layers of concentric circles breathe out of phase like water ripples, the feed inside the central phone mockup's screen auto-scrolls slowly, and white chips on both sides spring-pop in one after another and hover

cards.name: riso-print-hits
cards.summary: Misregistration impact frame: a single riso-misregistration-hit shot where the headline splits into two-colour riso plates the instant it slams to a stop, shakes twice and snaps into register with a "pop"
cards.use_when: Hit emphasis on headlines/cards, the paper-and-ink aesthetic's version of the "glitch flash"; a single-shot climax used 1–2 times per film
cards.duration: 4s (120f, single shot)
cards.energy: High
cards.intent: The RGB chromatic-dispersion glitch flash (part of impact-feedback variant C) is phosphor-screen language, and clashes with a paper-and-ink tone. This card offers a print-medium equivalent: the element splits into two single-colour riso plates (demo: fluorescent pink × blue; a multiply ink feel rather than a screen fluorescent feel, the two plates overprinting into a dark ink when registered), like a risograph with the plates out of register, shaking a few times before snapping into register with a "pop" — the same impact force, with the imagined medium switched entirely to ink on paper. Single shot: the plates split the instant of the sudden stop, the oscillation decays, and a hard cut snaps to register, stamping one hit. The demo is a video-shotcraft two-colour riso promotional poster ("CRAFT IT / LOUD." + three selling-point columns, with the single-colour-plate mirror-engraved logo at the centre of the round stamp).

styles.label: misregistration-hit — Single hit
styles.description: Print misregistration impact frame: riso-misregistration-hit single shot: at the moment the title hard-stops it splits into two-color riso plates, shakes twice and registers into place with a 'pop'
styles.use: A hit-stamp used 1-2 times per video; the moment a title / large text lands

cards.name: scan-bracket-sweep
cards.summary: A document pops into the centre, L-shaped viewfinder brackets drop onto its four corners, and a scanning light band trailing a gradient wake sweeps back and forth over the document for 5 passes — the document stays perfectly still throughout, and only the light reads it
cards.use_when: "Parsing/validating this content" process shots; capability demos for document products; the middle of an upload→analysis chain
cards.duration: about 5.0s (150f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium-low (mechanical and restrained; the rhythm lives entirely in the breathing of the back-and-forth sweeps)
cards.intent: Let the viewer understand "this thing is being read line by line by a machine". The viewfinder brackets first frame the target (announcing the object of inspection), and the scanning light band then travels back and forth across the whole page (announcing the inspection process). The crux is that **the document itself is completely still**: as soon as the document moves too, the viewer cannot tell whether it is "being inspected" or "loading".

styles.label: scan-bracket-sweep
styles.description: A document pops up at center, L-shaped viewfinder brackets drop onto the four corners, and a scanning light band with a gradient trail sweeps back and forth over the document for 5 passes; the document stays still throughout and only the light reads it

cards.name: scanline-annotate-focus
cards.summary: A scan line sweeps at constant speed from top to bottom over an already-existing page; as it crosses the lower edge of each block, that block is snapped into alignment by four-corner viewfinder brackets springing in from outside (one overshoot), after which a machine label typed out character by character is attached, and the status line at the top counts 00/06→06/06 in sync
cards.use_when: Analysis shots of "the AI is reading your page/brand"; teardown introductions of design systems/brand guidelines; self-explanation sections for product capabilities
cards.duration: about 5s (150f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium (mechanical and cool; the rhythm is driven by the constant-speed scan line, and the annotations are the beat points)
cards.intent: Turn the abstract act of "analysis" into a visible chain of cause and effect: wherever the scan line goes, that block is framed and named. The viewer reads "the machine's gaze", so the scan line must be constant-speed and the annotations must strictly lag the scan line's passage — **scan first, then snap the bracket**; once the order is scrambled it becomes a pre-choreographed animation.

styles.label: scanline-annotate-focus
styles.description: A scan line sweeps at constant speed from top to bottom over an already existing page; as it passes the lower edge of each block, that block is snapped onto by four-corner viewfinder brackets that spring inward from an expanded position (with one overshoot), then a machine label typed out character by character is attached, while the status line at the top counts 00/06→06/06 in sync

cards.name: scanline-assemble-flyin
cards.summary: The page opens on a blueprint artboard with only a grid and dashed slots while a bright scan line sweeps from top to bottom; as it reaches each slot, that component flies in from off-screen, overshoots and snaps into place, with a directional afterimage blur and snap-in corner marks on landing — by the time the scan finishes the whole page is assembled
cards.use_when: Openers where the "page generates itself"; the core demo of AI site-building/auto-layout products; capability narratives from blank to finished
cards.duration: about 5.2s (156f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium-high (the scan line is steady, but every component fly-in is a burst point, with density building up)
cards.intent: Give "the page being generated" a credible construction order: the scan line is the construction progress bar, and components flying in from off-screen to snap into place are the construction actions. The key is that **the last block is assembled exactly when the scan finishes** — if the scan line finishes early or the components trail behind, the cause and effect of "scanning drives assembly" falls apart.

styles.label: scanline-assemble-flyin
styles.description: The page opens as a blueprint artboard with only a grid and dashed slots, and a bright scan line sweeps from top to bottom; as it reaches each slot, that component flies in from off-screen, overshoots and snaps into place, with directional ghost-trail blur and a snap-in corner mark on landing, so the whole page is assembled exactly as the scan finishes

cards.name: slam-entrance-moves
cards.summary: Three high-energy slam-in variants: kanada-perspective-snap, a Kanada-style perspective sudden stop; score-slam, a score slamming down; impact-burst-kit, a landing-point impact kit (rippling out to neighbouring cards)
cards.use_when: Heavy-punch entrances for hero cards/KPI cards; impact-feedback handles the feedback after landing, while this card handles the case where the entrance itself is the impact
cards.duration: Per-variant action segment 6–22f + impact aftermath ~16f + hold ≥45f (demo: A 120f / B 135f / C 140f)
cards.energy: High
cards.intent: The ceiling of force in the library's entrance vocabulary has always been deck-deal-flyin's "dealing" — fast but not heavy. This card fills in the "slam" tier, in three flavours: A is a sense of direction — a card is flung in hugging the camera with fisheye-level exaggerated perspective, and flattens with a "pop", the swagger of the anime Kanada school; B is a sense of weight — a KPI card slams down from 2.6 times its size in front of the camera, with a ring + dust motes + screen shake trio detonating on the same frame, with the heft of a sports score pop-up; C is a sense of transmission — on top of B's trio, as the shockwave front sweeps over the left and right neighbouring cards it visibly pushes them away and lets them spring back, "this hit shook the neighbours", saying how strong the force is in a single move. Select by narrative need: to tell the viewer "it's coming" use A, "it's heavy" use B, "it shook the whole room" use C.

styles.label: kanada-perspective-snap
styles.description: perspective 300→1500px + rotate3d 58°→0 + scale 1.7→1 flung in over 18f, with a +5° overshoot flattening in the last 4f and the long slanted shadow straightening
styles.use: A single card's dashing debut; anime-leaning, light-hearted tone

styles.label: score-slam
styles.description: The card slams down from scale 2.5 / rotate 5° over six frames of Easing.in(quad), with a ring burst + dust particles scattering + screen shake all on the landing frame
styles.use: Heavyweight number entrances like KPI/score

styles.label: impact-burst-kit
styles.description: B's three-piece set + a shockwave front that sweeps neighbor cards on frames precisely computed from radius minus distance, with neighbor cards pushed out 30px + rotate ±3° and damped back
styles.use: 'Whole-scene shake' when neighbors already exist on the page

cards.name: spotlight-sweep-moves
cards.summary: Three dark-field spotlight-reveal variants: A wake-and-sleep sweep (bright where the light arrives, dark when it leaves), B edge-hugging glow lateral pan (purple light seeps in along the UI edge + the spotlight moves right at constant speed), C corner constant-speed reveal (a radial spotlight expands from the corner at constant speed and lights the whole screen); UI showcases where "light is the narrative" in a black field
cards.use_when: Introducing UI panels/functional areas one by one in dark-toned brand films; opening from black by "lighting up" the interface; light transitions between sections
cards.duration: 3.5–4.5s per variant; A/B can be chained into a tour section
cards.energy: Medium-low (restrained, mysterious, with the burst point at the instant of "lighting up")
cards.intent: In a black field the viewer can only see what the light shows — the spotlight is lighting as well as camera movement and editing: wherever the light goes things make their entrance, and when the light leaves they take their bow. The three variants share the identity element of the "edge-hugging purple glowing light line" (the light line runs along the UI border/logo/top edge, and the glow must be bright and diffuse, so that the light is "caressing" the interface rather than being a stroke animation). The crux is **constant speed**: the spotlight's movement/expansion is strictly linear — easing gives the light an "intention", and only constant speed reads as the mechanical sweep of a searchlight (precedent from the C variant: linear but with a final radius that is too large = saturation in the first 1/4, and it still does not feel constant-speed).

styles.label: glow-wake-sleep-panel
styles.description: Wake-and-sleep sweep: a radial reveal mask follows the light head moving left to right at constant speed, with a three-layer-glow purple light line along the top edge traveling with it, tracing light over the logo as it passes, lighting a vertical afterglow at the right edge, and in the final segment the panel sinks back into darkness
styles.use: Introducing a single UI panel in a dark-toned brand film: an entrance and exit that wakes and sleeps

styles.label: slide-spotlight-pan
styles.description: Edge-hugging floodlight horizontal pan: the light first travels around the top-left vertical edge, then after the corner runs horizontally along the top edge, with purple glow bleeding into the inside of the UI's top; the spotlight head moves right at constant speed to reveal while the panel slides left at constant speed = the feel of a camera panning right
styles.use: Horizontal tour of wide panels / multi-column boards, lighting up feature areas section by section

styles.label: corner-spotlight-reveal
styles.description: Constant-speed corner reveal: a radial spotlight from the top-left corner expands with a strictly linear radius, lit areas are revealed and unlit areas sink to black, and finally the full screen lights up; the light is the transition
styles.use: Black-field opening that lights up the interface for its entrance; light transition between sections

cards.name: autolayout-gap-dial
cards.summary: A gap dial drives the layout — a row of link blocks with a selection outline + gap spacing annotations, the badge number ticking up notch by notch, the blocks pushed apart in real time by the parameter and then springing back into place; a visualisation of "parameter-driven layout"
cards.use_when: The "change one number and the interface moves with it" selling-point shot for design-tool / low-code products; the category language of "packaging with design-tool semantics"
cards.duration: ~5s (150f: selection entrance + wind-up retract 10f + loosening 34f + held-breath hold 20f + spring rebound + settle hold)
cards.energy: Medium (tool-rationality type, the thrill lies in the locked synchronisation of number and displacement)
cards.intent: "The parameter changed, the UI changed" is the core promise of a design tool, but it is usually shot as a before/after comparison of "click the panel → cut to the result", with the causality cut out. This card shoots the causality as one continuous shot: the gap badge number ticks up notch by notch, the link blocks are pushed apart **on the same frame**, and the measurement line lengthens in real time — the number is the rein, the layout is the horse. The selection outline + 8 handles + gap annotations are all the native language of design tools, so the audience recognises at a glance "this is parameters being adjusted in a tool". The return deliberately uses an underdamped spring overshoot (shrinking tighter than the start and then settling), making "settling back into place" an elastic closing beat. Division of labour with type-and-filter: that is the search causality of "type content → list converges", while this card is the parameter causality of "dial a value → geometry rearranges".

styles.label: autolayout-gap-dial
styles.description: A spacing dial drives the layout: a row of link blocks with selection outlines and gap-spacing annotations, badge numbers ticking up step by step, blocks pushed apart live by the parameter and then springing back into place; a visualization of 'parameter-driven layout'

cards.name: canvas-materialize-moves
cards.summary: Two patterns for content "materialising onto the canvas" — panel-to-canvas row-to-card pour-out (panel table rows fly out along an arc and morph across containers into canvas cards) and diagram-cascade cascading generated tree (after the prompt is typed, nodes pop out layer by layer, with connector lines growing before the nodes)
cards.use_when: The narrative section of AI/collaboration tools where "generated results land on the canvas"; pattern A tells "existing content has changed its form of existence", pattern B tells "a structure grows out of one sentence"
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intent: The library's generation narratives are only "written out letter by letter inside a window" (document-typewriter-reveal, a document writing itself out) and "a chart comes alive by itself" (chart-live-moves); there is no vocabulary for **content leaving its container and materialising into a new entity on an open canvas**. This card fills that gap: the canvas is the stage, the generated objects are the actors taking the stage. The crux of pattern A is cross-container form migration — the same piece of content turns from a "row" into a "card", with position / width and height / corner radius / content layout interpolated in sync on one spring, so the audience reads "it flew over and changed" rather than "one deleted and one added"; the crux of pattern B is the cascade timing — a line draws out a node, a layer feeds the next layer, and the sense of structure comes from sequence rather than simultaneity.

styles.label: panel-to-canvas — Rows to cards
styles.description: Checkboxes tick automatically one by one → button press → three rows fly out with stagger along an upward-tossed arc, cross-fading from row form to card form in flight and landing with random tilt angles; the panel's row slots collapse into dashed empty space
styles.use: Bulk import / one-click place on board: content migrating from list state to spatial state

styles.label: diagram-cascade — Cascading generated tree
styles.description: Prompt types out character by character (outline darkens once typing finishes to confirm) → root (dark) → 2 children → 4 grandchildren pop in level by level, with elbow connectors drawing on 8f ahead of each level, and once the tree forms the whole tree breathes for one beat
styles.use: AI-generated structure/mind-map/ER diagrams: one sentence grows a tree

cards.name: chip-grid-single-select-blackout
cards.summary: Five option chips fade in one by one, centred in a 3+2 layout; on the selection frame a single frame of grey press block is inserted first, then within a few frames the fill turns ink black and the text turns white with a very light 1→1.04→1 rebound, while the other chips fade to 18% with their positions locked; afterwards the remaining ones go to zero, the black chip moves up and narrows, and the settled price rises below
cards.use_when: Interaction demos of single-select / plan / tier selection; the "what happens after you pick it" causality shot; price/parameter settlement chains
cards.duration: about 5.5s (165f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium-low (the only burst is that one grey-flash frame, everything else is pulling in)
cards.intent: One grey-flash frame + three frames of inversion to black takes the two-level `:active → :selected` states of a real UI and plays them apart. What the audience sees is "a finger presses down" and then "the system confirms", rather than a single gradient. The other chips drop to 18% while **their positions never move**: once they reflow, the audience would think the page refreshed, and the semantics of "single select" would be lost.

styles.label: chip-grid-single-select-blackout
styles.description: Five option chips fade in one by one, centered in a 3+2 layout; on selection a gray pressed block is inserted for one frame, then within a few frames the fill turns ink-black and the text turns white with a very light 1→1.04→1 rebound, while the other chips fade to 18% with positions locked; the remaining options then go to zero, the black chip moves up and narrows, and a settled price rises below it

cards.name: collab-cursor-moves
cards.summary: Collaboration cursors as actors — cast-ensemble, an ambient layer of five extra cursors (staggered fly-in + sine drift + a typing cameo + gathering to look on)
cards.use_when: Canvas scenes on collaboration / multi-user themes, laying "the team is here" warmth over the picture
cards.energy: A low-medium (an ambient layer, can underlay any duration)
cards.intent: Cursors in the library have always been "operating tools" (the cursor in cursor-flyover is a single-cursor click tour). This card promotes collaboration cursors carrying identity name tags to **actors**: five cursors enter in a stagger and then keep drifting as ambient particles, the sense of "the team is here" depends entirely on them, and one of them can even stop and type (a cameo role). An SVG cursor + name-tag chip is very cheap in cost and very high in narrative density, the cheapest visual argument for the "collaboration" theme.

styles.label: cast-ensemble
styles.description: Collaborative cursors as actors: cast-ensemble, an ambient layer of five extra cursors (staggered fly-in + sine drift + typing cameo + gathering to watch)
styles.use: Ambient layer across the whole video for canvas/whiteboard products; background liveliness when you need 'others are here too' beyond the main content

cards.name: glass-pill-dictation-typing
cards.summary: A fixed-width glass capsule pops in at about 1.25× slightly oversized and eases down into place, with a layer of accent-colour warm light spread inside it, faint on the left and dense on the right; the cursor leads, and a dictated sentence is then typed out at constant speed, the light (together with the ambient light behind the capsule) gradually receding with the typing progress, ending as a neutral frosted-glass bar
cards.use_when: The entrance of a voice/AI input box; an interaction-prompt shot for "talk to it"; a quiet transition beat between high-energy sections
cards.duration: about 3.3s (100f@30fps)
cards.energy: Low (the quietest beat in the film, only the light is receding)
cards.intent: Use "the light going out as input arrives" to tell one very small thing: while on standby it glows (waiting for you to speak), and the moment you open your mouth it yields the light to the text. In 3.3s it does only three things — pop in, type, the light recedes. Any extra motion (bouncing, colour change, icon animation) stops this beat from being a rest.

styles.label: glass-pill-dictation-typing
styles.description: A fixed-width glass pill pops in at about 1.25x size and eases down into place, with a layer of accent-color warm glow inside fading from light on the left to dense on the right; the cursor leads, then a dictated sentence types out at a constant rate, and the glow (along with the ambient light behind the pill) gradually recedes with typing progress, ending as a neutral frosted-glass bar

cards.name: hashtag-to-pill-materialize
cards.summary: A hashtag word typed into a physical object — "#word" is typed in the centre (red solid cursor constantly lit), a 1-frame hard cut turns it into a large wide capsule tag, after a hold it shrinks and moves left to land in the page's tag slot, then another 1-frame hard cut reveals the finished page; a rhythm skeleton of "two hard cuts and one slide"
cards.use_when: Demo sections for tag/category/keyword features (typing a tag in a notes app, topic aggregation); a three-part narrative of "input → becomes a UI object → settles into the finished piece"
cards.duration: 120f (4s) — typing ~40f + hard-cut capsule hold ~18f + shrink-and-move ~14f + rest of ~1.2s after the hard-cut reveal (original film 18–21.5s)
cards.energy: Medium (crisp and decisive, getting its drive from hard cuts, not from bounces)
cards.intent: The usual way to turn text into an object is a gradient/morph/expansion, but the frame-level breakdown of the original film proves Bear does the opposite: **the materialisation is a 1-frame hard cut** — the previous frame is still text + cursor, the next frame is a complete capsule, with no expansion, no cross-fade, no rebound. A hard cut gives the certainty of "snap, done", and any gradient softens "object" into "effect". The skeleton of the whole section is **two hard cuts sandwiching one slide**: hard-cut materialisation → smooth shrink-and-move into place → hard-cut reveal of the finished page. The only continuous motion (the shrink-and-move) is framed by two hard cuts, which is what makes it look both fast and steady. This rhythm skeleton is the crux: if the nature of any of the three moves is changed (turning a hard cut into a gradient, a slide into a hard cut), the whole card collapses.

styles.label: hashtag-to-pill-materialize
styles.description: Hashtag typing materializes: '#word' is typed at center (solid red cursor always lit), hard-cuts in 1 frame to a wide pill tag, and after a hold shrinks and moves left to land in the page's tag slot, then hard-cuts again in 1 frame to reveal the finished page; a rhythm skeleton of 'two hard cuts, one slide'

cards.name: picker-carousel-feature-cycle
cards.summary: A mobile-style vertical picker — the focus pill stays still while the content passes through it, each item decelerating with a clear outQuint snap and then holding completely still, with opacity/font size/greyscale controlled in layers by distance from the centre, and the pill doing a very light scaleY breath on settling
cards.use_when: List shots that read out feature names / scene names one by one; interaction demos of "pick one"; showing picker-type controls of mobile products
cards.duration: about 3.6s (108f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium (each snap is a beat point, advancing at a constant pace over 5 beats)
cards.intent: Build out the physical feel of "selecting": the focus frame is fixed, and it is the content that scrolls and gets snapped into place. After stopping, each item must **truly hold still for a few frames** — continuous scrolling reads as a loading animation, and only the pause reads as "this item has been selected". Distance falloff (opacity + font size + greyscale, three channels decaying together) is the only means of keeping the audience's gaze locked on the middle row.

styles.label: picker-carousel-feature-cycle
styles.description: Mobile-style vertical picker: the focus pill stays still while content passes through it, each item snapping with a clear outQuint deceleration then coming fully to rest, with opacity/font size/grayscale layered by distance from center, and the pill taking a very light scaleY breath on settling

cards.name: segmented-thumb-hero
cards.summary: The segmented-control thumb displacement as the protagonist close-up — an oversized capsule segmented control floats in on a spring, an outlined arrow cursor slides in from off-frame and presses, the white thumb slides to the other segment in 8f ease-out, and the instant it arrives the new icon springs out while the old icon retracts
cards.use_when: The announcement shot for a "mode switch / either-or" feature (the demo's video-shotcraft Prompt→Film, Chat→Agent style); a close-up approach where one UI micro-interaction carries a whole shot
cards.duration: ~3.5s (demo 110f: float-in 18f + cursor 24f + click + slide 8f + icon pop + hold)
cards.energy: Medium (a micro-interaction close-up, refined rather than booming)
cards.intent: When a product switches to a new mode, the usual way to shoot it is to swap out the whole interface. This card does the opposite: it enlarges the segmented control to 1080px wide for a close-up, and **the 8 frames of thumb displacement are themselves the narrative** — "we went from A to B". There is no page context at all, the control is the stage. The causal chain is complete: the cursor slides in (someone has arrived) → press + ripple (a decision is made) → the thumb slides (the world responds) → the new icon pops out (the new identity is established). None of the four beats can be missing: without the cursor the UI is just moving by itself, and without the icon pop the switch has no reward.

styles.label: segmented-thumb-hero
styles.description: The segmented control's thumb movement as hero close-up: an oversized pill segmented control springs in, an outlined arrow cursor slides in from off-screen and presses, the white thumb slides to the other segment with 8f ease-out, and at the moment it arrives the new icon springs out while the old icon retracts

cards.name: theme-switch-moves
cards.summary: Two patterns for theme switching — theme-sweep, a diagonal sweep across the field (reskinning in place wherever the boundary passes), and the palette-ripple combination (a ⌘K panel shrinks to a dot and a ripple spreads from that dot to reskin)
cards.use_when: Narrative sections on dark mode / theme features; the same UI "changing colour before your eyes" rather than cutting to a new scene
cards.energy: A medium / B medium-high (the combination has a complete causal chain)
cards.intent: Two ways of shooting a light/dark mode switch. A (the usual practice of Notion/Figma/Linear): a bright line on a 15° diagonal boundary band sweeps across the whole frame (the demo sweeps from the right, where the switch is, toward the left), and wherever the boundary passes the light colour turns dark **in place**, with the same layout in both themes coexisting for a moment — what the audience sees is "the same UI reskinned", not a transition. B (a combined variant): type "dark" in the ⌘K panel and press Enter, the panel shrinks into a bright dot, and a dark ripple spreads **from that dot** across the whole UI — the causal chain of "a command triggers the reskin" is complete and readable. The crux of the combination: the ripple's centre must be the panel's shrink point, and the start frame must be the frame where the shrink completes.

styles.label: theme-sweep-toggle
styles.description: The dark version's clip-path polygon sweeps the scene with a 15° slanted edge (out poly3, fast then slow ~38f), the boundary carrying a 4px bright white line + 18px glow that fades out over 2f after the sweep; the dark version's scale 1→0.995→1 settles it
styles.use: Direct demonstration of a theme feature

styles.label: palette-theme-ripple
styles.description: Panel drops in with back(1.9) spring → typing character by character → on Enter the panel contracts to 0 with ease-in + a white highlight core pinned in place → a circular clip expands from radius 12→1250px with cubic-out, the edge carrying a 5px white ring with glow in both directions
styles.use: Highlight segment linking a command palette with theme switching

cards.name: type-and-filter
cards.summary: Typing a search on the real UI, the grid converging by itself to a single card, and a click punching through into the detail page
cards.use_when: The "operation narrative" section of a feature demo; any interaction chain of search/filter/entering a detail page
cards.energy: Medium (an unhurried beat after the high-energy dealing section)
cards.intent: Let the audience "follow along and do it once": see clearly what was typed, how the page responded, and where was clicked. This is the only shot in the whole film that simulates a real person operating, and the rhythm must feel like a human hand, not a script.

styles.label: type-and-filter
styles.description: Typing a search into a real UI, the grid converges by itself into a single card, and a click passes through into the detail page

cards.name: voice-waveform-live
cards.summary: A recording capsule's live voiceprint — 64 thin vertical bars rise and fall with "speaking", tall in the middle while speaking and shrunk to a dotted line during pauses, the waveform scrolling from right to left; the full performance of speak → pause → speak → submit collapse
cards.use_when: Feature shots for voice input / AI assistants "listening to you speak"; sections with no UI content to show but needing sustained liveliness to hold up the picture
cards.duration: 172f (~5.7s: entrance 14f + speak 1.4s + pause 0.8s + speak 1.4s + submit collapse / tuck into bubble 0.8s + hold 0.7s)
cards.energy: Medium (functional liveliness, not showmanship)
cards.intent: This card is a **functional** voiceprint: a live receipt of "listening to you speak". The crux is causality: the waveform jumps with "the user speaking" and is the product's feature itself, not decorative packaging that jumps with the BGM. Tall while speaking, shrunk to a row of dots during pauses, history scrolling out to the left — the audience reads from the rise and fall of the waveform that "it is really listening", and a 6s+ picture is held up entirely by this liveliness, with no other content needed. Division of labour with gauge-readout-moves: a gauge is the mechanical ritual of "reporting a value", while this card is the vital sign of "continuous listening", with no final value.

styles.label: voice-waveform-live
styles.description: Recording-pill live waveform: 64 thin vertical bars rise and fall with 'speech', towering in the middle while speaking and shrinking to a dotted line during pauses, the waveform scrolling from right to left; a complete performance of speak → pause → speak → submit collapse

cards.name: brand-ink-open
cards.summary: Ink-line crosshair draws on → wordmark stamps in letter by letter → typewriter kicker → one full second of stillness, then lifts away and dissolves
cards.use_when: Brand opening; any title sequence that "establishes the name before entering the product"
cards.duration: about 2.8s (83f)
cards.energy: Low (starting position, leaves room for the following shots to climb)
cards.intent: The first beat gives the brand its memory hook: before any product footage appears, the audience clearly sees and remembers the name. Quiet, paper-and-ink texture, with one complete moment of stillness.

styles.label: brand-ink-open
styles.description: Ink-line crosshair draws on → wordmark stamps in character by character → typewriter subtitle → holds still for a full second, then floats up and dissipates

cards.name: crane-rise-reveal
cards.summary: Crane-rise reveal — the opening pushes in on a single row of data, then the camera decelerates upward along the Y axis and pulls back, rows flooding in until the whole dashboard fills the frame
cards.use_when: Establishing opening that goes "from detail to the whole"; the mirror opposite of drone-dive-landing (whole → single-point dive)
cards.duration: 5.5s (165f: close-up hold 24f + rise 102f + settle/aftermath/stillness 39f)
cards.energy: Medium-high (continuous one-way motion, no impact beat)
cards.intent: The library already has an establishing opening, drone-dive-landing — it slams from a god's-eye view into a hero close-up, "whole → focus". This card is its mirror image: "focus → whole" — first sit on one row of real data so the audience can see clearly "what this is", then pull back and up like a crane arm, rows of content flooding into the frame, until the whole product fills the screen — "the row you just saw is only one cell of this whole wall". Suits openings that sell on product scale / richness of content; use only one of the two directions in the same film.

styles.label: crane-rise-reveal
styles.description: Crane-rise reveal: opens tight on a single row of data, the camera rises along the Y axis with deceleration and pulls back, rows surge in until the whole dashboard fills the full frame

cards.name: dataviz-landscape-open
cards.summary: Dark-stage tributary-line landscape opening — many streamlines flow into a main trunk, made-up ID labels float on the lines, and the camera flies through at low speed with heavy depth of field
cards.use_when: Brand-level abstract opening (a "data universe" metaphor), followed by a bright-stage product section or the wordmark; division of labour with glow-flyline-moves: that card is the connecting-line narrative between cards within a section, this card is the full-frame landscape dedicated to openings
cards.duration: 5–8s (an atmosphere section for an opening, ≤1 per film; demo 180f)
cards.energy: Low opening, slow rise (starting position, leaves room for the later climb)
cards.intent: A brand-level opening category evidenced by the Linear Releases launch film opening: shoot the data world behind the product as a **dark-stage landscape** — bundles of tributary lines flow in from the depths of the frame into one main trunk (a metaphor for "countless workflows becoming one product"). The realism comes from three things: (1) made-up issue/task ID labels floating on the lines (the demo uses video-shotcraft shot numbers + camera-move names: each tributary is a shot, and together they form one finished film) (the audience recognises "this is the kind of thing I see every day"); (2) heavy depth of field — large out-of-focus near-field lines flowing past, mid-field labels sharp and readable, far field fading out, three layers of depth that make a flat SVG read as space; (3) the camera flies through low and steady — this is an atmosphere section, not a showpiece section, and the sense of speed is left to the shots that follow. Compliance basis for hand-built UI: this is not a replica scene (this picture does not exist on the page), so under the revised core principle 1 it is judged on the quality + clarity-of-expression bar.

styles.label: dataviz-landscape-open
styles.description: Dark-field tributary-flow landscape opening: multiple streamlines merge into a main trunk, fictional ID labels float on the lines, and the camera flies over slowly with heavy depth of field

cards.name: fracture
cards.summary: 5×5 tiles gather from a 3D shattered state into a whole poster, ring by ring in a ripple from the centre; after a beat with the lettering lit, all the fragments accelerate away from the centre, spinning, and fly off screen
cards.use_when: The first shot of an opening, a brand/poster reveal going "from chaos to form"; played in reverse, or using only the second half, it works as a hard transition
cards.duration: about 5.2s (156f@30fps; assemble 0–2.6s · hold 1s · scatter 1.5s)
cards.energy: High (high energy at both ends, still in the middle, suited to cutting in and out on BGM accents)
cards.intent: Film "the product taking shape" as a physical event: fragments fly back into place from three-dimensional space, each with its own spin, and the audience watches a complete picture grow out of disorder; after the hold to read the text, the whole thing then bursts off screen, handing attention cleanly to the next shot. Entrance and exit are symmetrical, so one piece of footage can be used in both directions.

styles.label: fracture
styles.description: 5×5 tiles reassemble from a 3D shattered state in rings by center ripple into a full poster, hold a beat while the text lights up, then all shards accelerate away from center, spinning out of frame

cards.name: icon-field-colorize
cards.summary: A dot-matrix of greyscale small icons surfaces in staggered fashion to fill the whole screen, holds for a beat, then several brand-colour horizontal bands ripple down extremely fast to flip the whole field — an opening/closing card of "lay out the full feature panorama first, then light up the brand in an instant"
cards.use_when: Opening that lays out the product's range of capabilities (icons = a universe of features) and then stamps on the brand colour in one stroke; feature-collection pages, ecosystem/integration scale displays, a lead-in pad before the title-sequence logo
cards.duration: surfacing ~45f staggered + rest ~10f + colour flip 12–45f + final-state rest; whole section 3–6s (demo 170f: colour flip on the 30f setting + title landing + final-state hold 1s)
cards.energy: Medium (the surfacing is set-up, the colour-flip moment is the only burst)
cards.intent: First use greyscale to lay out "many" in full — hundreds of small icons surface in staggered fashion to fill the frame, with greyscale ensuring they read as background texture and do not steal the scene; hold a beat so the audience realises "it's full", then the brand colour sweeps across the whole field extremely fast in the form of horizontal band ripples, and the grey world is lit up in an instant. The crux is that **the colour flip is not a hard flip on a single frame**: measured on the original film, several colour waves sweep downward in succession within ~0.5s (blue covers the whole field first, then orange/green/red in turn cover lower row bands), and the final state is layered in four horizontal colour bands — the ripple gives the "lighting up" a direction and a speed, while a hard flip merely reads as a swapped picture.

styles.label: icon-field-colorize
styles.description: A grid of grayscale small icons fades in with stagger to fill the full screen, holds a beat, then several brand-color horizontal bands ripple across and flip the whole field extremely fast from top to bottom; an opening/closing card for 'lay out the full feature landscape first, light up the brand in an instant'

cards.name: letterspace-materialize
