cards.summary: Wide-tracked wordmark crystallises through continuous all-character parallel drawing — every letter starts its stroke on the same frame, strokes grow continuously like handwriting, and all finish together on the same frame into the word; a brand wordmark developing over an atmospheric backdrop
cards.use_when: Brand wordmark entrance for the outro / opening (a wide-tracked thin skeleton wordmark; the demo is video-shotcraft in all lowercase); chapter titling; closing frames that need a serene / premium feel
cards.duration: rest ~15f + drawing ~50f + final-state rest ≥30f; whole section 3–4s
cards.energy: Low (a serene sense of ceremony, completed in a single breath)
cards.intent: The wordmark is neither a fade-in nor a typewriter but a "crystallisation": the strokes of all the letters begin growing continuously at the same time, like an invisible hand writing every letter at once, and they close together in the same instant into the word. Two crux points: **continuity** (the strokes must be a continuously drawn process, with no mask segmentation — doing half first and the other half after gets seen through; any intermediate frame should look like "half written"); **synchrony** (all letters start on the same frame and finish on the same frame — per-letter stagger carries typewriter semantics, while here it is the ceremony of the whole word as one).

styles.label: letterspace-materialize
styles.description: A wide-letter-spaced wordmark crystallizes by continuous parallel stroke drawing across all characters: all letters start on the same frame, strokes grow continuously like handwriting, and all close into the word on the same frame; the brand wordmark develops over an ambient background

cards.name: magician-card-flourish
cards.summary: On a midnight-blue dark stage a blue starburst flashes for 0.3s (X-shaped needle beams rotating 90° + a centre glow radiating small rays), and a card is fired out of the flash point — spinning extremely fast along an arc toward the camera, the spin decaying as it approaches, then an instant hard freeze (card height 86% of frame height), a light pulse + sheen sweep, and the copy on the right revealed line by line afterward
cards.use_when: A magical entrance for a single card/poster/cover (title-sequence key visual, product card reveal); pure black dark stage; a burst that needs the ceremony of "conjuring it out"
cards.duration: 156f (flash 0.3s + flight 1.6s + freeze/sweep/copy reveal + hold 3.3s; whole section 5.2s)
cards.energy: High (a one-off burst, still once frozen)
cards.intent: A magician flicking a card: a blue starburst flashes past, and the card seems to be conjured out of the light — fired from the extreme far distance at the centre of the frame (visually a small dot), it spins extremely fast along an arc toward the camera, and hard-freezes at the instant it reaches the centre into a near-full-frame display. Three crux points for the magic feel: **flash first** (the light is the ceremony of the "conjuring", 0.3s, short and crisp), **launch rhythm** (take off slowly to build force → suddenly accelerate and kick out → decelerate along the arc to arrive, slow-in → burst → decelerating arc), and **freeze means still** (no deceleration tail, no rebound; 13 whole turns of spin guarantee that the freeze lands exactly face-on).

styles.label: magician-card-flourish
styles.description: On a midnight-blue dark field a blue starburst flashes for 0.3s (X-shaped needle beams rotating 90° + center glow radiating small flares), and a card shoots out from the flash point, flying toward the camera on an arc with extremely fast self-spin that decays as it approaches, then hard-freezing instantly (card height 86% of frame height), with a light pulse + sheen sweep, and the copy on the right reveals line by line afterward

cards.name: orbit-ring-title-open
cards.summary: On a graphite dark stage, eight dark 16:9 content cards are evenly spaced at 45° on a 720×380 ellipse and revolve at constant speed (the card bodies never tilt; depth comes only from a ±12% scale given by sin θ, z-order, and distant dimming and defocus); while the ring expands, the card contents freeze on their first frame and all eight start playing together after f24; a centred two-tier title unblurs letter by letter and settles downward, and at the moment the keyword lands a fluorescent marker block sweeps in from the left to cover it, the letters inverting to ink as it passes, with a mono sub-line surfacing afterward; optionally in the last section the whole line defocuses and fades out, the ring still turning, handing off to the next shot
cards.use_when: The first shot of an opening = "this product has a whole set of things"; the front-of-house shot for a material library / template library / feature matrix / case collection; when you need real moving product footage to carry a statement, instead of arranging screenshots into a static nine-grid
cards.duration: 150f (5s@30fps; 2.9s of steady-state touring + a very slow push-in after the marker block lands at f64; with HANDOFF_EXIT on, the exit starts at f118 to hand off)
cards.energy: Medium (the only sustained motion is the constant-speed revolution, and the whole film has just one impact: the marker block's sweep)
cards.intent: When an opening wants to say "we have a whole set of things", the most common approach is to arrange screenshots into a grid — but a grid is static, and what the audience reads is "a pile of pictures", not "a set of moving products". This card turns the display into a **circular tour**: eight cards revolve at constant speed along an ellipse, always with cards entering the frame and cards leaving it, so the picture carries the implication of "there is more", while the title stays firmly pinned in the very centre, unaffected. The key trade-off is that **the card contents really play**. A static screenshot on the ring is only recognised as a "carousel"; with real motion running in the cards, the same ring immediately becomes "the product at work". But if all eight cards start playing at the same time, eight motions fight for the scene and none of them gets read — so during the entrance the card contents are **frozen on the first frame**, and start playing together only after the ring has expanded and the title has begun. The audience's attention order is therefore: first recognise this is a ring of product footage → read the title → only then notice that everything in the cards is moving.

styles.label: orbit-ring-title-open
styles.description: On a graphite dark field, eight 16:9 dark content cards evenly spaced at 45° revolve at constant speed on a 720×380 ellipse (card bodies never tilt; depth comes only from sin θ giving ±12% scale, z-order and dimming/defocus at the far side); while the ring spreads, card content is frozen on its first frame and all eight start playing together after f24; a centered two-level title deblurs and settles character by character, and the moment the keyword lands a highlighter block sweeps across from the left to fill it, the text inverting to ink where the block passes, then a mono subline surfaces; optionally in the final segment the whole line defocuses and fades out while the ring keeps turning to hand off to the next shot

cards.name: spotlight-hero-card
cards.summary: In a darkened theatre a tungsten spotlight (with a volumetric light shaft) sweeps across the page and locks onto one card; after an oblique push-in the card pops up and hovers, a champagne-coloured light beam traces its outline for two laps, and together with the 3D annotation it settles back into place
cards.use_when: A "single protagonist" style product opening; stands one core object (a card/entry/module) up as the lead of the whole film
cards.duration: 172f (about 5.7s; lock at f34 → touchdown at f142 → 30f of truly still hold)
cards.energy: Medium (the shot with the highest finish, slow and steady in rhythm)
cards.intent: The opening says only one thing: this one card is the atomic unit of the product. The spotlight guides the audience's gaze, the pop-up and hover give it volume and weight, the outline light beam is a metaphor for "scanning/inspecting", and finally settling back into place shows that it belongs to this page.

styles.label: spotlight-hero-card
styles.description: In a theater with the lights off, a tungsten spotlight (with volumetric light beam) sweeps across the page and locks onto one card; after an angled push-in the card pops up and hovers, a champagne-colored beam traces its outline twice, and it settles back into its original position together with the 3D annotations

cards.name: stroke-segment-build
cards.summary: Broken strokes become a word — the title is split into a dozen or so unconnected stroke segments that light up one by one in shuffled order, unreadable for the first 70%, and the moment the last segments land the meaning snaps into place
cards.use_when: A product name / big-number reveal in an opening that hangs on suspense; ≤1 per film; division of labour with type-assembly/draw-svg-trace: those are "watching the text be assembled/drawn", this card is "meaning revealed after a delay"
cards.duration: 165f (5.5s; 2s hold after the reveal at f105)
cards.energy: Low start, medium finish (suspense type, the landing frame is the energy point)
cards.intent: The precedent of the title sequence of Alien: the title is not drawn, it is "developed" — split into discrete stroke segments that light up in shuffled order, so for the first 70% of the time the audience sees only mysterious fragments, and the moment the last few segments land they suddenly read what the word is. "The moment of recognition" is the hook, and the strength of the hook depends on how long the unreadable period is sustained and how late the key segments are held back.

styles.label: stroke-segment-build
styles.description: Broken strokes into words: the title is split into a dozen or so unconnected strokes that light up segment by segment in shuffled order, unreadable for the first 70%, and at the moment the final segment lands the meaning snaps into place with a 'pop'

cards.name: text-as-mask
cards.summary: Text as a video mask — extra-bold headline letters are cut out of a porcelain-white stage, and a dark live product panel drifting slowly shows through inside the letters; at the end, after a held breath, the letterforms rush in exponentially and enlarge 46× to overflow the frame, the picture inside taking over the full screen
cards.use_when: An opening or chapter card that merges a brand word/slogan with product footage; the text is the door, the product is inside the door
cards.duration: 165f (entrance 18f + drift inside the text 78f + intake of breath 8f + rush-in takeover 24f + settle/hold 37f)
cards.energy: Medium-high (steady in the drift section, one burst in the takeover section)
cards.intent: Headline and product footage fighting for the screen is an old problem — text first and then picture is slow, picture over text is cramped. This pattern makes the two one body: the letterform is the mask, the product shows only through the strokes, the audience reads the word and the picture texture at the same time; at the end the letterform swells and overflows the frame, and the product naturally takes over the full screen — "walking from the brand word into the product" told in a single shot, doubling as a chapter transition (the same family as the transition-travel A letter-counter fly-through: there the camera drills into the counter, here the letterform swells by itself; the former is camera motion, the latter is door motion).

styles.label: text-as-mask
styles.description: Text as video mask: ultra-bold headline letters are cut out of a porcelain-white stage, with a dark live product panel panning slowly through the inside of the letters; at the end, after taking a breath, the letterforms scale up exponentially by 46x and overflow, and the picture inside takes over the full screen

cards.name: grain-dissolve
cards.summary: A whole line of text bursts into boiling grain noise and a diagonal-hatch selection box surfaces, then the noise cloud rapidly condenses into a larger, glowing short wordmark, with displacement decaying to zero and freezing in place
cards.use_when: A closing "XX. Now Live" style launch announcement; an energy-gathering beat that compresses a long sentence into a short brand mark
cards.duration: about 2.0s (60f@30fps; graining 0.26–0.56s · condensing 1.2–1.42s · solidify, fall back and finish)
cards.energy: Medium-high (a short, one-off energy pulse, a natural outro beat hit)
cards.intent: Film "a sentence condensed into a single word" as a physical event: the sentence first destabilises and boils into grain (the information disintegrates), the selection box implies "being selected and extracted", and then all the grain energy collapses toward the centre into a larger, brighter short wordmark — what the audience reads is "all of this boils down to it".

styles.label: grain-dissolve
styles.description: A full line of text bursts into boiling grain noise and a diagonal-hatched selection box appears; the noise cloud rapidly condenses into a larger glowing short wordmark, and displacement decays to zero and freezes

cards.name: logo-shrink-wordmark-lockup
cards.summary: A large neon cut-out ring quickly closes into a small solid white O at the centre, swapping to the video-shotcraft logo on the overshoot brake, the icon shifting left to make room, the wordmark letters sliding in one by one to complete the lockup, closed with an accent-colour tagline
cards.use_when: Brand styling at the end of a film: closing from full-screen graphic energy into a standard "icon + wordmark + tagline" lockup
cards.duration: about 4.4s (132f@30fps; closing 0.1–1.2s · making room 1.5–2.1s · letters 2–2.7s · tagline 3.2–3.7s)
cards.energy: Medium (the closing segment has impact, and the whole is a steady settling rhythm)
cards.intent: The "stamp" action of an ending: a full screen of neon ring collapses with energy into a small icon, heals its gap and turns pure white (from performance state to standard state), and then lands step by step according to the brand lockup specification — the icon makes room, the wordmark enters, the tagline closes things out. What the audience sees is the brand "standing firm" out of motion.

styles.label: logo-shrink-wordmark-lockup
styles.description: A large neon cutout ring rapidly contracts into a small solid white O at center and swaps to the video-shotcraft mark as it overshoots and brakes, the icon slides left to make room, wordmark letters slide in one by one to complete the lockup, and an accent-color tagline closes

cards.name: neon-triple-marquee
cards.summary: A three-row counter-moving neon marquee recap — giant hollow neon-tube letters of a three-word phrase fill top, middle and bottom of a brick wall shot at an angle, with odd and even rows rolling horizontally in opposite directions at constant speed without end, the three rows lighting up in turn at 1/3 phase offsets, and powering down row by row at the end
cards.use_when: A closing passage where theme words are repeated like a parrot; the "afterglow" treatment for a three-word slogan; a music section laid out with no narration
cards.duration: 4–5s (demo 150f: 18f row-by-row ignition power-up + loop body + 18f row-by-row power-down + 8f lights-out hold)
cards.energy: Medium-high (continuous flow + row-by-row pulses, no instantaneous impact)
cards.intent: A single-row marquee is just web decoration; stack up three rows, make odd and even run opposite ways, and let the brightness travel by phase in turn, and it becomes "the theme words marching in formation before the audience's eyes". The crux is the **light-dark round-robin**: at any moment only one row is the neon lead and the others are dimmed to thin outline background — all three rows fully lit is a signage accident, and lighting in turn is what makes a recap. The counter-rolling creates a "surrounded" feel: the top and bottom rows go right and the middle row goes left, the gaze is sandwiched in the middle with words flowing past endlessly from both sides, reading as "these three words cannot be said out".

styles.label: neon-triple-marquee
styles.description: Three-row counter-direction neon marquee recap: giant hollow neon-tube words in three-word chains fill top, middle and bottom rows across an obliquely shot brick wall, with odd and even rows scrolling horizontally in opposite directions at constant speed forever, the three rows lighting up in turn at 1/3 phase offsets, and powering off row by row at the end

cards.name: outro-group-photo-launch
cards.summary: Elements from the whole film fly in from all sides to pose around the wordmark for a group photo, with a crane landing camera position + stage light + gold dust making a launch-event close
cards.use_when: Outro / brand closing; a "family portrait" style final shot for a multi-feature product
cards.duration: about 4.8s (145f)
cards.energy: Peak (the highest point of the whole film)
cards.intent: Pick one representative element from each feature shown and call them back for a group photo, with the wordmark making its grand-finale entrance — what the audience remembers last before leaving is "these things belong to the same product". The specification must be launch-event grade: push the energy to the highest point of the film.

styles.label: outro-group-photo-launch
styles.description: Elements from the whole video fly in from all sides to surround the wordmark in a group photo, with a crane landing at the camera position + stage light + gold dust making a launch-event closing

cards.name: ui-strip-away-outro
cards.summary: A subtractive ending — after clicking Publish, the entire editor UI evaporates layer by layer in staggered fashion from the periphery to the centre, leaving on a black field only that one button, which slides to screen centre and enlarges, then fades out to hand off to the wordmark final
cards.use_when: An outro with "publish / done" semantics; a product ending that wants to say "after one click all the complexity disappears"
cards.duration: ~4.8s (144f: cursor into position 34f → evaporation ~40f → button alone → wordmark takes the baton → wordmark hold ≥1s)
cards.energy: Medium (quiet operation in the first part, continuous exit in the middle, no instantaneous impact)
cards.intent: All the endings in the library are "additive": outro-group-photo-launch has elements flying in for a group photo, and the logo sting holds still and then delivers an Easter egg. This card is the only "subtractive" route — the click detonates the exit of the whole UI, the black field keeps only the semantic focus (the button that was clicked), translating "publish = complexity zeroed" into a motion narrative. There are two crux points: **the evaporation must have order** — from the periphery to the centre one layer every 4f, each layer with its own directional displacement (each scattering off-screen), and out-of-order or all going out in the same frame reads as a power-failure glitch; **the button is the sole survivor and must migrate** — during the evaporation it slides from a corner of the toolbar to the screen centre, enlarges 1.5x, with a white halo strengthening as the black field does, completing the elevation from "UI control" to "ritual lead", and finally fades out to hand the black field over to the wordmark.

styles.label: ui-strip-away-outro
styles.description: Subtractive outro: after clicking Publish, the whole editor UI evaporates layer by layer with stagger from the periphery to the center, leaving only that button on black, which slides to screen center and scales up, then fades out to hand off to the final wordmark lockup

cards.name: ui-to-brand-morph
cards.summary: Two variants of UI becoming brand — icon-flip-bloom (the icon flips about the Y axis flat into a vertical line, then opens out from the line into the brand mark, with the amber bevel then sliding in) + wordmark settling character by character, and input-morph-assemble (the input box shrinks into the vertical stroke of a viewfinder, and three primitives drop into construction slots to assemble the complete mark)
cards.use_when: Brand closing / the last beat before the outro; the visual argument that "the UI you use every day is this brand"
cards.energy: Medium-high (an ending flourish, one complete transformation telling the whole story)
cards.intent: The brand-closing library already has two routes: brand-ink-open is an opening draw-on stamp, and outro-group-photo-launch is elements gathering around for a group photo (gathering without changing). This card adds a third: **product UI elements transform into the brand symbol by themselves** — variant A is an icon turning over to become the logo (an in-place entity swap), and variant B is the input box that appears repeatedly through the film gathering after the last send into the brand mark (a multi-element landing assembly). What the audience sees is not "the logo appeared", but "the thing we were just using turns out to be it", and the causal chain itself is the brand argument.

styles.label: icon-flip-bloom
styles.description: Icon wobbles twice with anticipation → squashes along the Y axis via scaleX into a vertical line (double-layer trail + blur) → swaps solid at the thinnest point, spring-unfolds into the video-shotcraft 'Jingke' mark, with an amber slanted cut sweeping in as a second beat → mark moves left to make room, wordmark settles character by character
styles.use: Single-icon products; where the icon and logo differ greatly in form and need the magic of 'flip over and transform'

styles.label: input-morph-assemble
styles.description: Cursor clicks send → text flies away → the input box's x/y/w/h/r five values spring-interpolate into the mark's vertical frame → top and bottom bars and the amber slanted cut land one after another from a dashed construction box to assemble the 'Jingke' mark → moves left to make room, wordmark settles character by character
styles.use: Films where a rectangular UI like an input box/card is the main character; the logo can be broken down into a combination of geometric primitives

cards.name: beat-cut-moves
cards.summary: Hard cuts as a beat instrument — burst-flash freeze: three white flashes each hard-cut to a different crop of the same picture (wide → card → close-up), and after the shutter afterglow settles it stops on the close-up to close
cards.use_when: Highlight sections that play the "cut" itself as a drumbeat; the ceremony of an awards-style burst of shots, the crowning of key information
cards.duration: whole run 140f ≈4.7s (live footage 30f + three flashes + hold 70f)
cards.energy: High
cards.intent: The library's rhythm vocabulary has only ever governed the rate "within one movement" (speed-ramp-freeze freezes then thaws within the same take) and "how long to stop after settling" (the R-series breathing precedents), with no word for **how to lay out the cut points between shots**. This card fills that gap: hard cuts with no transition of any kind, where the interval between cut points is itself the score — three white flashes, with intervals tightening (22f→18f), reading as a camera's burst shutter (A). It does not conflict with the R-series: R governs the stop after settling, this card governs the layout of cut points, and when the string of cuts ends it must be followed by enough hold to hand the breathing back. Note that this is a deliberate exception — the rhythm-preference precedent is one-way "slow down", and the harder the cut string cuts, the longer the hold after the cuts must be than usual.

styles.label: paparazzi-flash — Flash-burst freeze
styles.description: Hard cuts as a beat instrument, flash-burst freeze: three white flashes each hard-cut to a different crop of the same frame (wide shot → card → close-up); after the shutter afterglow settles, it holds on the close-up to close
styles.use: Ceremonial highlight moments: award-show burst shots, crowning a key number

cards.name: beat-step-list-theme-cycle
cards.summary: A three-channel metronome — in a dark field an adjective list steps up one row per beat, a fixed capsule at the centre of the viewport "catches" the next word and changes colour, and the whole field's base colour changes on the same beat; the row, colour and field channels are locked to the same beat point
cards.use_when: Sections on "the same product in many moods / multiple themes" (a run of adjectives in the modern/playful/expressive style); the densest-rhythm section of the whole film; sections that hit the beat of the music
cards.duration: lead-in 30f + 18f per beat × number of beats + closing hold; 4 beats about 4.7s (demo 140f)
cards.energy: High (one beat every 0.6s with three channels jumping together, density-type high energy)
cards.intent: Changing a theme colour once is a feature demo; changing it every 0.6 seconds, three times in a row, with "the selected row + capsule colour + whole-field base colour" jumping together on the same frame each time — that is a metronome. The cheapest variable switch is used to create the highest rhythmic density in the whole film. There are two crux points: first, **the three channels must be locked to the same beat point**, and if any one channel is half a beat slow, "jumping together" degrades into three animations each doing their own thing; second, **the boundary between jump and slide** — the jump takes only the 6f at the head of the beat and the remaining 12f are completely still; a beat point must "jump" not "slide", and a list scrolling at constant speed is just a list.

styles.label: beat-step-list-theme-cycle
styles.description: Three-channel metronome: on a dark field, an adjective list moves up one row per beat while a fixed pill in the viewport center 'catches' the next word and changes color, and the whole background color switches on the same beat; row, color and field channels are locked to the same beat points

cards.name: panel-grid-moves
cards.summary: Panel rhythm — comic-panel-split: comic diagonal panels split out three camera angles of the same subject, and after the three panels click-click-click into a freeze, the last panel's diagonal edge swallows the screen into a poster
cards.use_when: Treating "panels" as a rhythm device: several camera angles of the same subject frozen side by side, split out panel by panel on the beat; feeds on beat points
cards.duration: 156f ≈5.2s (full-screen profile shot 20f + three-cut panel split freeze + swallowing the screen + poster hold)
cards.energy: Medium-high
cards.intent: The difference from wall-reveal-moves is this card's positioning anchor: that one is "how the whole wall enters" (a one-off reveal), this one is "how panels act as a rhythm device" — the panel split happens on the beat, a panel change is a drumbeat. A is a merge: the picture is split open by three diagonal seams going click-click-click, three camera angles of the same product freeze at the same time, and after a beat the last panel's diagonal edge sweeps across and swallows the whole screen — the split-screen language of Scott Pilgrim. Suited to a single product from multiple angles (demo: a prime lens engraved with video-shotcraft, three narration boxes numbered "Shot 01 / 02 / 03", and after swallowing the screen it lands as the "Craft the shot." poster).

styles.label: comic-panel-split
styles.description: Panel rhythm: comic-panel-split, diagonal comic panels cleave out three camera angles of the same subject, three panels freezing in click-click-click, then the last panel's diagonal edge consumes the screen into a poster
styles.use: Side-by-side multiple viewpoints of one subject; comic-flavored segments

cards.name: quad-split-parallel-scenes
cards.summary: The picture hard-cuts to a 2×2 four-way grid, with the four quadrants running their own micro-scenes in parallel (typing, a sudden push-in, word by word, an interaction chain), the key beats offset by 3–6 frames to create an information bombardment
cards.use_when: A montage beat for rhythm sections where "there are many features, all happening at once"; the density peak in the middle of a trailer
cards.duration: 90f (3s@30fps: 0–62f parallel bombardment + 28f final-state hold, no transition throughout)
cards.energy: High (four parallel lines + staggered-beat impacts, the standard BGM chorus slot)
cards.intent: Replace sequential display with parallel density: four things happen before the eyes at the same time, the audience has no time to read each in detail, but every 3–6 frames one quadrant "moves" — the scanning rhythm is firmly pinned down. This is a technique card: the contents of the cells are all replaceable, and the staggered-beat choreography is the recipe.

styles.label: quad-split-parallel-scenes
styles.description: The picture hard-cuts to a 2×2 quad split, with the four quadrants each running their own micro-scene in parallel (typing, crash zoom, word by word, interaction chain), key beats offset by 3-6 frames to create an information barrage

cards.name: rhythm-interrupt-moves
cards.summary: Interrupting the rhythm — jump-cut-punch-in, a three-step jump-cut push-in: the same composition hard-jumps to a larger scale three times with no tweening, closing in on the target level by level
cards.use_when: Using "interrupting continuity" itself as the rhythm device: a stop-start push-in (A); complementary to beat-cut-moves (cut-point layout)
cards.energy: A medium
cards.intent: The library's rhythm cards all govern "how to cut and how densely"; this card governs **how to break** — the audience expects continuity, and you interrupt it instead, so the way of interrupting is the expression: A is a spatial break — the same composition jumps larger three times with no tweening (1x→1.6x→2.6x), the stop-start of a Godard jump cut, giving more of a commanding "look here, closer, that's the one" than a continuous push-in. Suited to forcing focus on a metric.

styles.label: jump-cut-punch-in
styles.description: Rhythm interruption: jump-cut-punch-in, a three-step jump-cut push-in: the same composition hard-jumps larger three times with no tweening, closing in on the target level by level
styles.use: Closing in on a core metric level by level; documentary-style fixation

cards.name: sakuga-timing-shift
cards.summary: From shooting on threes to shooting on ones — an element first moves in flip-book stop-start steps of one step every 3 frames, and at the climactic instant switches to a frame-by-frame silky sprint; the frame-rate-quantised sudden change is itself the point of interest
cards.use_when: Emphatic movement of a single element (a card entrance, a metric crossing the line); sections that need the contrast of "handmade feel → climactic burst"
cards.energy: Medium-high
cards.intent: The library's time-axis manipulations already include speed-ramp-freeze's freeze-and-thaw and hit-counter's local frame hold. This card is a different one — **what changes is not the speed but the frame rate itself**: in the stop-start section the driving frame is q=floor(f/3)*3, so the element moves only one step every 3 frames (a 10fps flip-book), and from the switch frame it is driven frame by frame by the raw f, a silky sprint. The dullness of shooting on threes and the smoothness of shooting on ones are cut against each other on the same screen, the beat-count staging of Japanese animation (shooting on 3s / on 1s). The stop-start section does not feel low-grade but handmade, and the switch point is the climax marker.

styles.label: sakuga-timing-shift
styles.description: On threes to on ones: the element first moves in flipbook stutter at one step every 3 frames, then at the climax switches to a smooth frame-by-frame sprint; the frame-rate-quantized abrupt change is itself the point of interest

cards.name: speed-ramp-freeze
cards.summary: A rhythm technique of non-linear frame-number remapping — freeze annotation (flow → freeze, circle and annotate → thaw)
cards.use_when: In a card stream / long sideways move, "stopping one key point to show people"; teaching explanations, review contexts
cards.duration: freeze annotation whole run 158f (≈5.3s, freeze section 67f ≥45f)
cards.energy: Medium-high (the speed contrast is itself the energy beat)
cards.intent: A constant-speed stream reads as PPT (R2), and a fast stream throughout leaves the audience unable to catch the key point (R3). Freeze annotation, within a single movement, simply stops — a marker circles the key point and then it moves on. The technical root is frame-number remapping (slope is rate), and the semantics are "stop the class and underline the key point".

styles.label: freeze-annotate
styles.description: A rhythm technique using nonlinear frame-number remapping: freeze-frame annotation (flowing → freeze and circle callout → unfreeze)

cards.name: trailer-grammar-moves
cards.summary: One pattern of trailer grammar — trailer-bumper, a front-loaded rapid-cut hook: three shots in a 9f rapid cut + a beat of black-screen silence, then the opening title
cards.use_when: The opening hook of a trailer (cold open): stuff in the three most eye-catching shots before the main feature, then a beat of silence before the formal opening
cards.energy: A high
cards.intent: Each of the library's rhythm cards governs one segment: beat-cut governs cut-point layout, rhythm-interrupt governs interruption. This card governs **the structural moments of a trailer** — not how any one shot moves, but how the joints of the whole film connect: A is the opening hook — before the main feature, 0.9 seconds stuffed with the three most eye-catching shots in rapid cut + a beat of black-screen silence before the opening, the "preview" of a trailer.

styles.label: trailer-bumper
styles.description: Trailer grammar, style one: trailer-bumper, a front-loaded fast-cut hook: three shots cut fast at 9f each + a beat of silence on black, then the opening title
styles.use: A hook before the main feature opens; cold open

cards.name: bottom-push-stack-wipe
cards.summary: Bottom-edge push-up chapter change: the new scene, background colour and all, pushes in full-screen from the bottom edge and physically shoves the old scene out of frame; several chapters are pushed in a row, each with its own saturated background colour, and the content is pinned into each chapter's own coloured coordinate system and travels with the background
cards.use_when: The chapter-change skeleton of multi-chapter product films (one selling point and one background colour per chapter); section cuts that need a "page-turning rhythm" running through the whole film
cards.duration: demo triple push 170f (~5.7s); a single push-in 26f + in-chapter hold ~1.2s
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intent: wipe-transitions is a boundary sweeping across, with neither old nor new page moving; page-turn is the old page splitting like double doors and sliding out. This card is a third physicality: **the new chapter shoves the old chapter out** — two screens in rigid contact, displacing at the same speed in the same direction, like a vending machine pushing a stack. The crux is "the whole screen travels with its background colour": the background colour + window card + decorative bars are welded into one block of material pushed in from the bottom edge, so the viewer reads "a different world" rather than "a different card". A heavy ease-out (fast in, slow stop) gives the push-in a "clunk" of landing; the 40px seam shadow on the upper edge is the evidence of the physical contact between the two screens. With three chapters pushed in a row and the background saturation maxed out, the chapter change itself becomes the film's metronome — the original slack film relies on this one trick alone as its skeleton.

styles.label: bottom-push-stack-wipe
styles.description: Bottom-edge push for chapter changes: the new scene, background color included, pushes up from the bottom edge as a full screen and physically shoves the old scene off frame; several chapters push in succession, each with its own saturated background color, and the content is pinned to each color field's coordinate system and travels with it

cards.name: card-flip-reveal
cards.summary: Feature-card 3D flip reveal: the card flips 180° about the Y axis, the front UI catches a light that moves with the angle as it passes the thinnest point on the side edge, and the back reveals a large conclusion number, with the cards sweeping across the whole row one at a time, staggered
cards.use_when: Paired "feature → result" storytelling: a row of feature cards each flipping out its own metric/conclusion in turn; an element-level transition card
cards.duration: 150f in total (~5s, including hold); per card 4f wind-up + 16f flip + ~10f spring settle, three cards staggered by 12f
cards.energy: Medium-high
cards.intent: The library already has wipe-transitions' blinds in the "flip" family (blades flipping one by one, about changing pages). This card is a **semantic flip**: the two faces of a card are a cause-and-effect pair — the front is the feature interface, the back is the numeric conclusion it brings. The flip action itself is the answer to "so what?", the standard grammar of Apple's bento sections. Sweeping a row one card at a time with a 10f stagger, three cards and three numbers read as "results reported in succession".

styles.label: card-flip-reveal
styles.description: 3D flip reveal of feature cards: each card flips 180° around the Y axis, a highlight that moves with the angle grazes the front UI at the thinnest point on the edge, and the back reveals a large conclusion number; cards flip with stagger, sweeping across the whole row

cards.name: card-flock-tumble
cards.summary: Three UI page cards tumble in 3D from their thin side edges and settle into a staircase (clear throughout, spline-continuous and silky smooth), keep rotating slowly after settling without stopping, then are quickly drawn into the centre, blasting out a single turbulent smoke ring that spreads, with giant type sweeping across to close
cards.use_when: Energy climax sections (an explosive transition from a group of feature pages → the brand slogan); neon/aurora dark-field tone; sections where "multi-page capability" is condensed into a single line
cards.duration: tumble ~1.5s + slow-rotation display ~0.3s + collapse 0.3s + smoke ring + giant type ~2s; whole section 4.5s
cards.energy: Extremely high (use for the energy peak of the whole film)
cards.intent: Three page cards tumble and line up in 3D space like playing cards flung out; after settling and showing themselves they are instantly drawn into the centre, blast out a ring of smoke, and the giant brand type bursts out through the ring — "capability showcase → energy collapse → slogan eruption" in one breath. There are three crux points: **silky smooth** (side edge → tumble → settle is a single Catmull-Rom spline with continuous derivatives, and the hitch of piecewise interpolation will be seen), **no stopping** (after settling, keep a low angular velocity and rotate slowly until the collapse; a still section was rejected with "don't stop, keep rotating" — a climax section has no still frames), and **clear throughout** (motion blur/depth-of-field haze all deleted, rejected with "don't add blur effects").

styles.label: card-flock-tumble
styles.description: Three UI page cards tumble in 3D from their thin edges and settle into a staircase (sharp throughout, smooth spline-continuous motion); once settled they keep rotating slowly, then rapidly converge and get sucked into the center, burst into a single turbulent smoke ring that expands, and giant text sweeps across to close

cards.name: circle-match-iris
cards.summary: Circle-centre-matched iris cut: the iris bursts open from the centre of a circular element on the page, and the circular chart of the new page inside the iris connects onto the same circle; the match cut gives the iris a semantic anchor
cards.use_when: Seams where the foreground has a circular element (avatar/icon/round button) and the background has a circular subject (donut chart/ring progress); a transition technique card
cards.duration: 5.5s / 165f (entrance + eye-catch 40f + wind-up 7f + circle-join iris opening 37f + sweep 58f + still 47f)
cards.energy: Medium-high
cards.intent: An ordinary iris (the vocabulary list's original entry) opens from any point, and the viewer reads only "the page changed". This card welds it to a match cut: the iris must burst from the centre of a **real circular element** in the foreground, and the new page growing inside the circle has a circular chart that joins onto exactly the same circle — what the viewer sees is "the avatar's circle becomes the chart's circle", and the circular form itself completes the narrative (this person → this person's data). This is the landing form of the match cut in a UI context: it relies not on a coincidence of composition, but on a semantic circle-to-circle. Like the three traversal variants it belongs to "the background is already present inside the foreground", but the anchor is an abstract shape rather than a container.

styles.label: circle-match-iris
styles.description: Circle-center match iris cut: the iris bursts open from the center of a circular element on the page, and the circular chart on the new page inside the iris continues from the same circle; the match cut gives the iris a semantic anchor

cards.name: gradient-transition
cards.summary: The background transitions smoothly between three kinds of CSS gradient, linear, radial and conic — angle, colour stops, centre and radius interpolated parameter by parameter, with a cross-fade between segments to change type
cards.use_when: Continuous variation of ambient backgrounds/chapter background colours; giving static typographic sections a "living" background layer
cards.duration: about 6.7s (200f@30fps; linear 0–2.3s · radial 1.9–4.4s · conic 3.9–6.7s)
cards.energy: Low (pure background motion, making way for foreground content)
cards.intent: A gradient is not a static texture but an animatable parameter set: any parameter within a gradient of the same type can be interpolated into a silky-smooth change, and across types a short cross-fade bridges them. Used as a background layer, it gives sections with "no subject motion" a layer of continuous low-speed energy.

styles.label: gradient-transition
styles.description: The background transitions smoothly between linear, radial and conic CSS gradients, interpolating angle, color stops, center and radius parameter by parameter, with cross-fades between segments to change the type

cards.name: line-carry-transition
cards.summary: Line-relay lateral transition: scene A's progress bar extends out of frame, the camera follows the line sideways, and the line turns corners in motion to enclose scene B's card frame, with no cuts throughout
cards.use_when: Between two scenes with a graphic kinship (progress bar → card frame, underline → chart axis); the signature transition slot of a film, the graphic relay of the Catch Me If You Can title sequence
cards.duration: ~6.3s / 190f (progress bar fills 36f + bursts out 10f + lateral move 56f + frame closes 24f + poster in the frame 30f + still 24f)
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intent: The transition library's three big families (traversal/hidden cut/block) all answer "how does the scene change"; this card's answer is **it doesn't change at all — a line leads you across**. After the progress bar fills, its end extends into a long line that bursts out past the card edge, the camera follows the line sideways 1920px into the new world, and the line turns right angles in motion to enclose scene B's card frame; the frame closes and the content fades in, and from start to finish the viewer's eyes never leave this line. Graphic continuity is itself the transition. The difference from match-cut: that is shapes lining up on either side of a cut — a cut after all; this is continuous drawing — **there is no cut**. The line's identity needs a narrative logic (the progress bar "finished", so it extends outward); a line with no reason is just decoration.

styles.label: line-carry-transition
styles.description: Line-relay lateral transition: scene A's progress bar extends out of frame, the camera tracks the line sideways, and while moving the line turns corners to frame scene B's card, with no cuts throughout

cards.name: mosaic-reframe
cards.summary: 12 tiles morph continuously between three layouts, a regular grid, a feature mosaic and a diagonal cascade string, with position, width and height each interpolated, a slight stagger tile by tile, and a hold between segments
cards.use_when: Display transitions of "many ways of seeing the same batch of content": layout-capability showcases for portfolio/template-library/album products
cards.duration: about 7.1s (214f@30fps; emerge 0–22f · hold A · A→B 56–92f · hold B · B→C 132–176f · hold C to 214f)
cards.energy: Medium (continuously flowing rearrangement, no burst point, a calm temperament)
cards.intent: Let the viewer see "the layout itself thinking": the same 12 pieces of content go from a tidy archive state (grid) to a curated state with primary and secondary (feature mosaic), and then to a dynamic state with attitude (diagonal cascade).

styles.label: mosaic-reframe
styles.description: 12 tiles morph continuously between three layouts (regular grid, feature mosaic, diagonal waterfall strings), with position, width and height each interpolated and slight per-tile stagger, and a hold between segments

cards.name: page-turn-transitions
cards.summary: Whole-page block transition: barn-door-split, a double-door curtain split (the old page splits into two halves and slides out, the new page rises to meet it)
cards.use_when: Chapter-level page changes: the "turning the page" ritual between two big sections where old gives way to new; division of labour with the shot-transitions family (shot hand-offs) — that is "the aerial camera moving over", this is "the page is itself a physical object"
cards.duration: single variant 150f (establishing the prior state 30–40f + transition 24–40f + follow-through and close ≥70f), about 5.0s
cards.energy: Medium-high
cards.intent: The three variants of shot-transitions and transition-travel/hidden-cut all treat the page as a "scene" — the camera moves between scenes. This card treats the page as a **physical object**: it has thickness, has weight, and can split open. The ritual feel of the block metaphor is stronger, suiting chapter-level big page changes (feature A finished → feature B) rather than small shot-level hand-offs. The barn door is "the old yielding" — the old page tears open from dead centre and slides away, and the new page rises to meet it from underneath, implying replacement, dedicated to old-for-new succession.

styles.label: barn-door-split
styles.description: Whole-page block transition: barn-door-split, a double-door curtain split (the old page splits in two and slides out, the new page rises to meet it)
styles.use: Old-to-new handoff: before/after a redesign, plan A → plan B

cards.name: print-texture-transitions
cards.summary: Print-texture transition: ink-bleed-reveal, where a whisker-like bleeding edge spreads and eats up the old scene
cards.use_when: The paper-and-ink aesthetic version of a scene-change seam; the third family alongside the three hand-off variants/the traversal variants — the "medium developing" type of transition
cards.duration: 4–4.5s (bleed segment 55–80f + still close ≥30f)
cards.energy: Medium (gradual emergence, no impact beat)
cards.intent: The transition vocabulary already has hand-offs (the three variants of shot-transitions) and traversal (transition-travel) , both spatial/optical metaphors. This variant opens the third family: **the medium metaphor** — the new picture does not "arrive" but is "printed/dyed" in, directly invoking the physical imagination of the library's paper-and-ink aesthetic: like a drop of ink landing on rice paper, bleeding out and eating up the old scene, organic and calligraphic. It has a natural affinity with films in the paper/ink tone, and is another "medium-family" seam choice besides light-leak-burn (accent-colour light leak).

styles.label: ink-bleed-reveal — Ink-bleed reveal
styles.description: Print-texture transition: ink-bleed-reveal (whiskery bleeding edges spread and consume the old scene)
styles.use: Replacing old scene with new scene; handwritten feel, narrative tone

cards.name: shot-transitions
cards.summary: Three shot hand-off variants — push-in white flash, whip-pan (hard-brake version), mask-wipe through a window (depth version) — selected by energy drop and seam semantics
cards.use_when: Any junction between two shots (a technique card; after the shots are laid out at the storyboard stage, pick one variant for each seam)
cards.duration: n/a (technique card; the frames each variant occupies are in the parameters table, carved out of the adjacent shots' budgets)
cards.energy: n/a (technique card, takes no energy slot)
cards.intent: The library's shot cards only handle their own entrance and close, and "how shots are joined" has never had a vocabulary — a bare cut at a seam lets all the cinematic feel built up shot by shot leak away at once. Launch films widely regarded as excellent (Linear Releases/Agent, reverse-engineered from extracted frames on 2026-07-11) have not a single bare cut throughout: scene changes rely either on depth travel, or on focus relay, or on black-field title cards to build up force. This card collects three variants: a white flash covering the cut, a whip-pan borrowing blurred frames to change scene, and punching through a window into a detail world.

styles.label: flash-cut — Push-in white flash-cut
styles.description: The outgoing shot's camera pushes in, and the cut point straddles a layer of white flash that covers the page swap
styles.use: Page-to-page with interaction pass-through and similar energy (already in the library, folded in)

styles.label: whip-pan — Whip pan
styles.description: The camera whips sideways in one beat to the next scene, with motion blur smearing the middle section to unrecognizable and the scene change hidden in the blurred frames
styles.use: Rapid-fire fast-paced feature segments (a light high-energy → high-energy option, saves frames and speeds up compared to style B)

styles.label: mask-wipe — Window pass-through
styles.description: A real element on the page (a card) scales up into a full-screen window, and the new scene grows from inside the window and takes over
styles.use: Semantic seam: feature overview → that feature's detail ('open this card to enter its world')

cards.name: tear-streak-transitions
cards.summary: Tear transition: glitch-displace, a noise tear (a hard cut in the middle of 16 horizontal strips jittering out of register), a strip-level tear with digital-glitch semantics
cards.use_when: High-energy page changes: digital glitch/rupture semantics; a strip-level tear where the page's integrity is not broken and the energy is maxed out
cards.duration: prior state ≥40f + tear 16–24f + close ≥40f, about 4.5s (135f)
cards.energy: High
cards.intent: This card handles the **strip-level tear** — the page is cut into horizontal strips moving at high speed, but each strip's content is complete. This is a taste boundary drawn by repeated rulings: the fragment-type transitions were rejected three times in a row (doom-melt vertical strips falling, pixel-dissolve squares flipping to black, facade-block bricks flying, all eliminated), while the strip type passed. Fragments read as "the page is being destroyed", strips read as "the page is moving at high speed" — integrity not broken, yet energy maxed out. Horizontal tear: strips jitter left and right out of register + a two-colour silhouette ghost (a restrained version of RGB split: two single-colour silhouettes of the same page's content, using only the picture's two accent colours, offset by ±12px). Suited to system-glitch/instant-jump semantics — the demo uses it for the state jump of "a release console going from Rolling out 99% to is live".

styles.label: glitch-displace
styles.description: Tear transition: glitch-displace, noise tearing (a hard cut in the middle of 16 horizontal strips jittering out of position), strip-level tearing with digital-glitch semantics
styles.use: Glitch/rupture semantics; a violent page swap before the climax

cards.name: transition-hidden-cut
cards.summary: Three hidden-cut-point transition variants — foreground-occlusion invisible cut, collision screen opening, warm light leak — with the hard cut hidden inside 1–3 frames of occlusion/impact/light peak so the viewer cannot see the scissors
cards.use_when: When a junction between two shots needs a "traceless scene change" or a "ceremonial screen opening" (a technique card, selected at the same level as the three variants of shot-transitions)
cards.duration: n/a (technique card; the frames each variant occupies are in the parameters table, carved out of the adjacent shots' budgets)
cards.energy: n/a (technique card, takes no energy slot)
cards.intent: Of the same family as shot-transitions variant A flash-cut: flash-cut uses a layer of white flash to cover a hard cut, and these three variants swap in three kinds of "blinder" — a foreground card sweeping past (A), the impact frame of a collision (B), and a light leak climbing to its peak (C). The shared principle is magician's misdirection: the hard cut is completed during the 1–3 frames when the viewer's eyes are drawn away by a large movement/strong light, and by the time they look back the scene has already changed, with "the scissors invisible" throughout. Flash-cut is the plainest option; choose A for a sense of direction, B for a sense of ceremony, C for warmth.

styles.label: invisible-cut — Foreground-occlusion invisible cut
styles.description: An oversized card with heavy motion blur sweeps across the face, and within the occluded frames where the blur fills the whole screen the background hard-cuts A→B; the card flies out and the viewer thinks it is still the same shot
styles.use: Page-to-page where the scene change should leave no trace; the main option for faking a 'one take'

styles.label: versus-slam — Head-on collision opener
styles.description: Left and right halves of the screen with slanted edges accelerate in from off-screen and collide head-on; the impact frame has a white flash + screen shake + a VS stamp, and the cut point is the impact itself
styles.use: Opener or chapter header with comparison/versus semantics (old vs new plan, two products, before/after)

styles.label: light-leak-burn — Amber light leak
styles.description: Three soft amber lights sweep diagonally, and when the light peak frame has swallowed about seventy percent of the old page it hard-cuts to the new page; by the time the light recedes the new page is already in place
styles.use: Chapter transitions wanting a warm / film feel; softer than a white flash, with direction and warmth

cards.name: transition-travel
cards.summary: Traversal transition: letterform-cavity traversal — the letterforms of a giant chapter title are themselves a window, and the camera dives into the letter strokes to complete the scene change
cards.use_when: Seams where the two shots have an "element/container"-level spatial relationship (a technique card, selected as a complement to the three variants of shot-transitions)
cards.duration: n/a (technique card; demo 150f, main push action segment 52f, hold before and after counted separately, frames carved out of the adjacent shots' budgets)
cards.energy: n/a (technique card, takes no energy slot)
cards.intent: The three variants of shot-transitions are the "hand-off" type — the previous shot closes and the next shot enters, with the seam relying on a white flash/blurred frames/ a window to cover the instant of the page change. This card is the "traversal" type — the background exists inside the foreground picture as a real element (a hole in a letterform), and the camera dives in with one continuous spatial movement, so that the viewer follows the same object from start to finish, with no hand-off instant. Selection rule: if the background can be "pre-sent" in the foreground → traversal; if the two scenes are merely in sequence with no spatial nesting → hand-off. The semantics of letterform-cavity traversal are "the title is the door" (chapter title card and transition in one).

styles.label: letterform-zoom — Letterform fly-through (letterform-zoom)
styles.description: Fly-through transition, letterform fly-through: the letterforms of a giant chapter title serve as a window, and the camera drills into the glyph strokes to complete the scene change
styles.use: Chapter title → body content; a high-energy alternative to style D's black-field text card

cards.name: white-flash-logo-simplify-cut
cards.summary: A liquid-metal-textured colour wordmark rests with flowing light, and after a wind-up a white flash blasts out from the centre of the letters in an overexposure; when the exposure falls back, the same position holds the flat version of the wordmark — one white flash completes the texture downgrade
cards.use_when: Closing a brand section (ornate showpiece → clean finishing); a transition beat where the mood switches from showing off to a formal announcement
cards.duration: about 4s (120f@30fps; showpiece 0–34f · wind-up 34–46f · white surge 44–54f · exposure fall-back 54–76f · lock 72–96f · hold to 120f)
cards.energy: Medium-high (a single pulse-like accent, with stillness before and after)
cards.intent: First give ample ornateness (iridescent liquid metal flowing across the letters, one diagonal highlight sweeping past), then use a single white flash to "purify" it into a flat single-colour wordmark — what the viewer reads is "the performance is over, and this is its formal image". The downgrade is a rhetorical device: switching from sensory texture to rational recognition. The two versions share the same font size and position, reading as "the same wordmark purified", not as a different picture swapped in.

styles.label: white-flash-logo-simplify-cut
styles.description: A liquid-metal-textured colorful wordmark rests with flowing light, and after building up energy a white flash blows out from the center of the letters in an overexposure; as exposure falls back, the same position holds a flat version of the wordmark, one white flash completing the drop from textured to flat

cards.name: wipe-transitions
cards.summary: Geometric wipe transition: blinds-slice, a venetian-blind strip cut (12 3D blades flip in a staggered wave, and after the wave sweeps through the whole page changes from A to B)
cards.use_when: A general-purpose transition where neither old nor new page moves and a geometric boundary sweeps through to complete the hand-over; does not depend on the composition having a suitable element, so it can be used anywhere
cards.duration: prior state ≥20f + wipe ~56f + close ≥40f, about 4.4s (132f)
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intent: The transition library already has three families: traversal (dive in), hidden cut (cover the cut), and block (the page is a physical object). This card is the fourth family, **geometric wipe** — neither old nor new page moves, and a geometric boundary sweeps through to complete the hand-over, with the shape of the wipe being the semantics: the strip sweep is "venetian-blind blades flipping one by one to change the page". The difference from shot-transitions C-variant window punch-through (an element-mask wipe): C uses a real element on the page as the mask (depending on the composition), whereas this card is a pure geometric shape — its generality is its positioning. Suited to lateral progression and page-turning semantics.

styles.label: blinds-slice
styles.description: Geometric wipe transition: blinds-slice, venetian-blind strips (12 3D slats flip with stagger into a wave, and once the wave sweeps through the whole page changes from A to B)
styles.use: Page-turn / push semantics; pages with a horizontal reading flow

cards.name: blur-slide
cards.summary: Title enters word by word, with y 0.38em→0 + blur 18→0 + opacity 0→1 converging together on one shared ease-out, about 4f between words; the subtitle follows in a staggered overlap before the title has finished settling
cards.use_when: Almost any place where a title and subtitle come as a pair; product-page hero copy, section subheadings; the default text reveal when you want "professional but not stealing the scene"
cards.duration: about 4.0s (120f@30fps)
cards.energy: Low (a single convergence, no peak, no loop)
cards.intent: This is the **default solution** for text reveals: no spectacle, no mechanical feel, just words being placed softly one by one. Its professional feel comes from a single thing: the y, blur and opacity channels share the same progress `p` and the same easing, so words "surface out of defocus" rather than "slide in with a fade on the side". When a film already has another heavy-handed technique (scramble / roller), the titles should use this card and give way to the lead.

styles.label: blur-slide
styles.description: Headline enters word by word, with y 0.38em→0 + blur 18→0 + opacity 0→1 converging in sync on the same ease-out curve and about 4f between words; the subtitle follows with stagger before the headline finishes

cards.name: brace-expand
cards.summary: A pair of small curly braces pressed tightly together appears at dead centre, then springs left and right with one overshoot and scales up to title size; the text clip width is strictly bound to the inner edges of the braces, revealing the text from the middle like a curtain being pulled open, and after settling the letter-spacing relaxes slightly
cards.use_when: Title cards for developer / technical products; chapter openers; a minimal single beat that needs "one symbol to do the reveal"
cards.duration: about 4s (120f@30fps: cursor 0–6f → 6f small braces hard cut → 14f spring open → 40–64f letter-spacing relaxes → subtitle → hold)
cards.energy: Medium (the single overshoot is the only peak, everything else is still)
cards.intent: Among title reveal techniques, this card is the most economical: no mask bars, no per-character, no displacement — only a pair of braces moving apart, with the text being "bracketed out". It carries a code feel by nature (`{}` are curly braces), so in a technical product context it reads as "this is the content itself". The crux is that the clip width **must be strictly bound to the brace positions**: once the text fades in or wipes in by itself, the braces degrade into decoration and the curtain feel is entirely lost.

styles.label: brace-expand
styles.description: A tight pair of small curly braces first appears at center, then springs apart left and right with one overshoot and scales up to headline size; the text's clip width is strictly bound to the braces' inner edges, revealing from the middle like a curtain being drawn open, and after settling the letter-spacing relaxes slightly

cards.name: countdown-arc-scatter
cards.summary: Nine equal-sized numerals on a paper dial are arranged tangentially along a large arc; the whole dial sweeps through 96° then decelerates to a hard stop, the "5" stops at the top of the arc and immediately translates into place as the first character of the title, while the other numerals scatter away in place with blur, the title fades in word by word with blur, and the last word turns to the accent colour
cards.use_when: Countdown / duration-promise copy ("5 min to install"); a data-reveal beat; short shots on a light background that need a "dashboard" vocabulary
cards.duration: about 3.3s (100f@30fps: sweep ~30f + landing 20f + title assembly + hold 22f; can be compressed to a 33f single beat at minimum)
cards.energy: High (a 96° large sweep squeezed into ~20 frames, pure impact)
cards.intent: "Installs in 5 minutes" written as a static title card, nobody believes it. The dial sweep puts that number inside a **range**: 45, 35, 28, 22, 17, 10 sweep past one after another and stop at 5 — the audience sees "from a lot to very little", and the number argues for itself. After stopping, the "5" does not vanish but **translates to become the title's first character**; one element completes the identity switch from instrument to copy, which is the most valuable move on this card.

styles.label: countdown-arc-scatter
styles.description: Nine equal-size numbers on a paper dial are laid out tangent to a large arc; the whole dial sweeps through 96° then decelerates to a hard stop, '5' stops at the top of the arc and then translates into place as the first character of the title, the other numbers disperse in place with blur, and the title fades in word by word with blur, the last word turning to the accent color

cards.name: document-typewriter-reveal
cards.summary: A full-page, properly typeset document window floating in a dark field "writes" itself out behind a cursor, the sidebar follows, history entries drop one by one into the track, and the camera pulls back from an oblique close-up of the title to the full window
cards.use_when: Feature shots for documents / reports / notes; the beat with the highest information density
cards.duration: 150f (about 5s, including the history-list-stack tail and the tagline hold)
cards.energy: Low-medium (highest information density, with the rhythm held steady so viewers can read the text)
cards.intent: The audience will read every word on screen — the persuasiveness of this shot rests entirely on "the document is real". The typewriter-style write-in turns a static page into a "document being written out", and the sidebar history entries dropping in add the time depth of "continuous output".

styles.label: document-typewriter-reveal
styles.description: A fully typeset document window floating in a dark field 'writes' itself behind a cursor, the sidebar follows, history entries drop one by one into their track, and the camera pulls back from an angled title close-up to the full window

cards.name: flying-words
cards.summary: 22 keywords are laid out by the golden angle on a flattened elliptical cross-section, flying along the z axis from far away to brush past the camera, with opacity following a [0,1,0.5,0.2,0] life curve, running exactly 2 full cycles for a seamless loop
cards.use_when: A dynamic background for keyword clouds / capability lists; an "information volume" underlay for openers and closers; a transition that needs a sense of flying through depth
cards.duration: about 6.0s (180f@30fps, 2 full loops, can be joined seamlessly)
cards.energy: High (continuous full-screen 3D displacement, no moment of stillness in the frame)
cards.intent: The crudest way to list keywords is to pile a screen of static word cloud. The word tunnel **spreads the same set of words along the timeline**: spawned far away, growing from small to large, brushing past the lens and disappearing; the audience only ever reads three or five words, yet the subjective impression is "lots of words". It is a background layer, not a lead layer — the camera stays still and the elements move, so overlaying a title or UI in the foreground causes no fight at all. Replace the whole word list with the project's keywords without changing a line of motion logic.

styles.label: flying-words
styles.description: 22 keywords are laid out at the golden angle on a flat elliptical cross-section and fly along the z axis from far away to brush past the camera, with opacity following a [0,1,0.5,0.2,0] lifecycle curve, running exactly 2 full loops with a seamless start and end

cards.name: glitch-cycle
cards.summary: One row of monospaced slots cycles through 4 status phrases, each with its head and tail on probability keyframes [1,0,0,0.1,0,0,1] going fully garbled and the middle with occasional single-character jitter, with RGB split and whole-row displacement layered on at the switch instant; the last phrase's probability falls to 0 so the ending is clean
cards.use_when: Status announcements for loading / build / deploy processes; the "system self-narration" in technical openers; a stretch of underlay that needs a machine voice to move time forward
cards.duration: about 5.6s (168f@30fps; in the demo each phrase is 38f, with the last phrase continuing to the end of the film as the closing hold)
cards.energy: Medium-high (continuous high-frequency noise pulses, the switch points are the peaks)
cards.intent: The clumsiest way to announce status is four lines of text fading in one after another. The cycle compresses them into **one slot**: the head and tail of a phrase "melt down" and then "solidify" through garbled characters, with the middle almost clean and only occasionally twitching — what the audience reads is "the system advancing step by step", not four independent pieces of copy. Garble density is the grammar of this card: dense = switching, thin = settled in this state. A progress bar at the bottom strings the four beats into one timeline, and the last phrase takes the probability to 0, so settling is the end.

styles.label: glitch-cycle
styles.description: A single row of monospace slots cycles through 4 status phrases; at the head and tail of each, a probability keyframe [1,0,0,0.1,0,0,1] fully scrambles the characters, with occasional single-character jitter in the middle, and the moment of switching adds RGB split and whole-row displacement; the last phrase's probability is set to 0 so the ending is clean

cards.name: gradient-word-sweep
cards.summary: In a tagline on a black ground, the keyword is swept rapidly from left to right by a gradient colour light and "charged" — the glow is strongest on the wavefront characters and decays backward, and once filled, thin purple-red lightning links the characters while the whole word breathes a steady-state bloom
cards.use_when: Charging up a single verb / selling-point word in a tagline (Supercharged/faster/AI…); the text moment in an energy-climax section; the slogan frame of a brand film on a black field
cards.duration: sweep-charge ~15–20f (must be fast) + steady-state lightning breathing 1–2s; whole section 2.5–3.5s
cards.energy: High (a one-word burst point, with everything before and after giving way)
cards.intent: In a whole sentence of white text only the keyword is "powered on": a gradient colour light sweeps rapidly across the characters from left to right, like energy being injected — brightest at the instant of sweeping past (the wavefront trail), then decaying to a steady state; once filled, thin lightning leaps between the characters, and the word keeps a breathing bloom. Three crux points: **fast** (sweep-charge 15–20f, slower reads as a progress bar), **brightest wavefront** (the freshly lit characters have the strongest effect, without this gradient it is just a static gradient crop), **restrained glow** (AE-style multi-layer bloom but do not smear it into a mass; lightning that is thin and sparse is what makes it an accent).

styles.label: gradient-word-sweep
styles.description: On a black-background tagline, a keyword is swept quickly from left to right by a gradient light and 'charged up': characters at the wave front glow strongest and decay behind it; once filled, thin purple-red lightning links the characters and the whole word breathes with a steady glow

cards.name: lead-word-zoom-assemble
cards.summary: The first word occupies the centre of the frame at 2.3x font size and keeps pushing in 6% during the hold, then a single curve simultaneously completes "shrink back to final font size" and "slide the whole line left into place", with the following words each pushed in from 0.5em to the right of their slot; the pivot is pinned horizontally to the first word's centre and vertically to the baseline (measured at mount), the subline surfaces in the same time window as the whole line moves up, and after a beat of stillness the whole scene crash-zooms in, defocusing, to hand off
cards.use_when: "Introducing" title cards for a brand / product name; the second shot of a launch-event-style opener; cases where a one-line claim needs "one word to fill the frame first, then the whole sentence filled in"
cards.duration: about 2.8s (84f@30fps; sentence assembly completes at f36, move-up and subline f32–46, stillness 26f, final 12f crash)
cards.energy: Medium-high (opens with a full-frame large word, but only one movement throughout, no secondary impact)
cards.intent: The easiest mistake with a title card is "the whole sentence fades in together" — the audience receives 5 words at once and remembers none. This card turns reading order into **physical order**: first give only one word, and make it so large it fills the frame and is still pushing toward the audience, so the audience is forced to read it first; then this word retreats to its own size and position within the sentence, and the whole sentence grows around it. By the time it settles the audience has already read the lead word twice. The real crux of the feel is not the scale curve but the **pivot**. The lead word travels from "dead centre of the frame" to "the position of the third character in the line"; if the pivot is taken at the line box centre, the scale and the left slide each pull the text in opposite directions, and in the last few frames the baseline shakes visibly to the naked eye. Pin `transform-origin` horizontally to the lead word's centre and vertically to the baseline; with these two points fixed throughout, the whole line simply "shrinks", with no drift at all.

styles.label: lead-word-zoom-assemble
styles.description: The first word takes the center of the frame at 2.3x font size and keeps pushing in 6% during the hold; then a single curve simultaneously completes 'shrink back to final font size' and 'slide the whole line left into place', with each following word pushed in from 0.5em to the right of its slot; the pivot is pinned horizontally to the first word's center and vertically to the baseline (measured at mount), the subline surfaces in the same window as the line moves up, and after a beat the whole scene hands off with a crash-zoom push-in and defocus

cards.name: marker-underline-title
cards.summary: After the big title settles, a marker underline beneath the keyword is drawn rapidly from left to right — a variable-width pen shape, rough edges, a slight upward slant following the italic text's momentum, hugging the bottom of the letters
cards.use_when: Emphasising a single keyword in a title (new/free/AI…); a handwritten / human-touch brand tone; annotation-style emphasis in body text
cards.duration: pen down 4~8f after the title settles, underline stroke 8–12f, 1–1.5s in total
cards.energy: Low (one stroke to finish the point, not stealing the title's scene)
cards.intent: A single hand-drawn marker stroke suddenly appears in a printed-type title, using the contrast of materials to pull one word out of the typesetting — like a person circling the key point on a poster with a pen. Three crux points: **fast** (8–12f in one go, slower reads as a loading bar), **close** (hugging the bottom of the letters, farther away it reads as a divider rather than emphasis), and **following the text's momentum** (the underline of an italic word must slope slightly up, low on the left and high on the right — drawing the slant the wrong way is the easiest mistake to make and an instant giveaway, see Known pitfalls for the precedent).

styles.label: marker-underline-title
styles.description: After the headline settles, a marker underline is quickly drawn from left to right beneath the keyword, with a variable-width nib, rough edges and a slight upward slant following the italic type, hugging the bottom of the text

cards.name: outline-word-fill
cards.summary: A hollow word (thin warm-grey outline, weight 500) lands from a 3.2x sharp-then-slow shrink, a large dashed circle then closes in from 2.8x to surround the word and rotates slowly, with horizontal dashed lines extending inward from the frame edges left and right; the outline brightens slightly first, then a solid white-hot fill hard-cuts on within one frame, a flash of glow, and it freezes
cards.use_when: A hammer-blow beat for a single-word benefit / slogan; a "nail" shot on a rhythm hit; an emphasis frame in a brand film on a dark ground
cards.duration: about 3.0s (90f@30fps, a short single beat + 36f settle)
cards.energy: High (3.2x shrink + instant light-up, short high impact)
cards.intent: To drive a word in like a nail, what works is not a slow fade-in but **two settlings**: first a huge hollow word shrinks rapidly into place (the settling of size), then the outline turns solid white within one frame (the settling of texture). The 1.5s of dashed-circle shrink and horizontal dashed-line extension in between is a "aiming" process — a technical drafting vocabulary that makes the light-up read as "confirmed". The fill **must be instantaneous**: a slow sweeping fill turns the nail into a slow beautifying animation.

styles.label: outline-word-fill
styles.description: A hollow word (thin warm-gray outline, 500 weight) shrinks from 3.2x with a fast-then-slow ease and lands; a large dashed circle then contracts from 2.8x to surround the word and rotates slowly, with horizontal dashed lines extending inward from the frame edges left and right; the outline brightens slightly first, then the solid white-hot letters hard-cut on within a single frame, and one flash of glow freezes

cards.name: paper-title-card
cards.summary: A single sentence is stamped onto the paper word by word, one word marked in accent-colour italic, closed off with a short dash
cards.use_when: Chapter transitions / value-proposition title cards; a lead-in card before an important feature appears; a breathing spot in the film
cards.energy: Low (a breathing spot, separating two high-energy shots)
cards.intent: Between two product shots, give the audience a one-sentence breather: state clearly "what to look at next and what it is worth". The letterpress stamping texture puts the title card in the same world as the paper-and-ink style product shots.

styles.label: paper-title-card
styles.description: A sentence is stamped onto paper word by word, one word set in accent-color italic, closing with a short dash

cards.name: pill-chip-slot-cycle-handled
cards.summary: In a white-ground sentence "Your `chip` Handled", the word inside a dark capsule rotates like a vertical roller, the capsule width stretching and contracting smoothly by interpolating pre-measured text widths, the text on both sides naturally pushed apart and drawn back, with grey ghost items at 13% opacity showing above and below the capsule
cards.use_when: "We handle ___ for you" style selling-point sentences; a one-line wrap-up of a SaaS feature list; the key-visual beat of a brand film on a light ground
cards.duration: about 5.0s (150f@30fps: rest → 3 switches (0.25/0.47/0.69) → tail rest)
cards.energy: Medium (a steady three-beat rhythm, with the width stretching the only continuous motion)
cards.intent: There are two schools of word-slot rotation: make the sentence dodge the change (a fixed-width roller), or make the sentence **accept** the change (the capsule widens and the text on both sides is pushed apart). This card is the latter; the cost is that the widths must be calculated accurately, and the payoff is a sentence that reads as alive — "Your" and "Handled" are pushed along, and the audience feels the word inside the capsule has weight. The grey ghost items showing above and below are the second marker: they signal explicitly that "this is a list that can roll", making the audience expect another word to come.
