styles.label: pill-chip-slot-cycle-handled
styles.description: In a white-background sentence 'Your `chip` Handled', the word inside the dark pill rotates on a vertical wheel, the pill width stretching and shrinking smoothly by interpolating pre-measured text widths so the text on both sides is naturally pushed apart and drawn back, with gray ghost items at 13% opacity showing above and below the pill

cards.name: pill-slot-cycle
cards.summary: Mid-sentence word-slot rotation — the sentence stem is pinned and does not move, and the pill badge at the end of the sentence rolls one notch like a slot machine every ~0.7s (the old one flies up accelerating and fading out, the new one slides in from below with blur), switching through N feature words in a row before landing as a complete sentence to close
cards.use_when: The most elegant solution for "feature listing" copy (faster than a list item by item, more semantic than character-level rolling); passages with a one-line selling point + multiple verb phrases
cards.duration: entrance 12f + 21f per beat × word count + closing 14f + hold; 6 words about 6.7s (demo 200f, including a 48f complete-sentence hold)
cards.energy: Medium (a steady metronome, no peak)
cards.intent: To list six features, a list needs six rows, and fading in item by item needs six beats and fills the screen. Word-slot rotation packs them into **one slot of one sentence**: the stem "One skill to ___" (the demo is about video-shotcraft: Storyboard it → Capture the page → Move the camera → Cut on the beat → Design the sound → Render the film) is the promise, each pill rolling through the slot is the evidence, and finally the pill flies away and "do it all." lands — the evidence is listed in full, and the conclusion is stamped. The structure carries three acts by itself: promise → listing → closing. The crux is that the stem **stays absolutely still**: the audience's eyes are pinned on the slot throughout, and if the stem so much as wobbles the listing feel falls apart.

styles.label: pill-slot-cycle
styles.description: In-sentence word slot cycling: the fixed sentence stem is pinned in place while the pill badge at the end rolls one notch like a slot machine every ~0.7s (the old one flies up accelerating and fading out, the new one slides in from below with blur), and after cycling through N feature words it settles into the complete sentence to close

cards.name: text-column-converge
cards.summary: Two-word confrontation then closing together — the left "NEW" and the right feature word are pinned at equal screen margins on either side and hard-cut through a rotation with zero shrinking throughout, and only at the last word does a single ease-in-out slide bring them to the centre to snap together into a phrase, with the small text underneath surfacing almost as a hard cut; a closing reveal-type text card
cards.use_when: Passages where a feature list closes on a product name / slogan (a "NEW × a string of features → NEW <product name>" pattern); launch-event-style recaps, version-number reveals
cards.duration: rotation 7–16f/word × 8–9 words + closing together ~36f + rest after the small text; about 5–6s for the whole section
cards.energy: Medium-low (a machine rhythm, the temperament of a small-type spec list, not slamming words)
cards.intent: Two words sit opposite each other on the left and right like a contents page, and the audience thinks it is just a rotating caption; only when the last word comes to rest do they discover that the left and right were actually two halves of the same sentence — the single continuous closing together retroactively makes the whole rotation a "build-up of suspense". The crux is **pinning**: during the rotation the two words do not move a single pixel, and the left and right screen margins are exactly equal (measured from the original film as 412 vs 413@1280); any gradual shrinking spoils the closing together in advance and dilutes the reveal into a progress bar. The closing together may happen only once, and it must come after the last word — this is a closing reveal, not a sustained motion.

styles.label: text-column-converge
styles.description: Two-word standoff converging: on the left 'NEW' and on the right a feature word, pinned at equal screen margins on either side and hard-cut rotating with zero shrinkage throughout; only on the last word, one single ease-in-out slide to center snaps them into a phrase, with small text below fading in almost as a hard cut; a closing reveal-type text card

cards.name: title-demote-to-label
cards.summary: Two variants of a big title demoted to a section label — A: the big title is revealed centred and holds a beat, then continuously shrinks 0.3x and translates to the top-left corner to settle as a small section label, with the content area growing beneath it; B: the same routine but on entrance a text-selection highlight block sweeps in and is then withdrawn
cards.use_when: Chapter openers (the title is the lead first and then gives way to the content); section handovers in tutorial / feature-demo films; variant B gives "text / editing" products an identity hint
cards.duration: A ~3.7s (112f) / B ~4.5s (134f); in the demo the two variants play in series for 246f
cards.energy: Low-medium (a layout-transform type, an atmosphere shot)
cards.intent: The usual fate of a chapter title is "appear → disappear → content enters", with the title and content not knowing each other. This card makes the title **demote without leaving**: the big centred text holds a beat to announce the topic, then a single continuous tween shrinks it to 0.3x and flies it to the top-left corner, where it settles as this section's column label — it is still on screen, only changed from lead to door plate. The audience gets free spatial memory: that big word just now is the small word at the top-left now, and this section is about it. The content skeleton begins growing while the demotion is still under way, so the handover has zero gap.

styles.label: title-demote-to-label
styles.description: Two variants of demoting a big title to a section label: A, the big title develops at center and holds a beat, then continuously shrinks by 0.3x and translates to the top-left corner to settle as a small section label while the content area grows beneath it; B, the same routine but on entrance a text-selection highlight block sweeps in and is then removed

cards.name: type-assembly-moves
cards.summary: Three text-assembly variants — split-text-stagger (characters split and rise one by one), letterform-drift-assembly (drifting together), text-on-path (flowing in along a line)
cards.use_when: Entrances of big titles / taglines; belongs with type-entrance-moves and document-typewriter-reveal to the same big category of title entrances, at most 2 kinds per film
cards.duration: single variant 4–5.5s (action segment A ~56f / B ~104f / C ~110f; demo full length including hold: A 130f / B 150f / C 160f, each exporting its own `*_DURATION`)
cards.energy: A medium / B medium-high / C medium
cards.intent: Title entrances already have an "in-place transformation family" (character drop / typewriter — characters change form where they stand). This card adds the "assembly family": characters **converge into** the title from elsewhere, and the motion trajectory itself has drama. A is the piano-key type — each character slides up from below an invisible clip line, rational and crisp, with the highest generality; B is the title-sequence type — characters drift in scattered with blur and lock one by one and deepen, the ritual feel of Stranger Things, suited to a brand-name reveal; C is the semantic type — characters file in along a rising curve and then straighten up, and the curve can trace exactly along a chart growth line, with text and data telling the story in the same frame.

styles.label: split-text-stagger — Split rise
styles.description: Each character translateY(115%→0) inside an overflow box with 10% overshoot, delay i×2f, with the baseline growing in sync
styles.use: General default; crisp and rational

styles.label: drift-assembly — Drift assembly
styles.description: Characters drift in from seeded directions of ±300px + blur 8px and settle into place with stagger, a deepening pulse on the lock frame, and after assembly the whole word breathes at 1.04
styles.use: Brand name / title-sequence-level debut

styles.label: text-on-path — Flow along path
styles.description: Characters slide in single file along a Bezier curve (rotating to the tangent angle), then straighten to horizontal over 12f after arriving
styles.use: When the curve carries meaning (growth line / process line)

cards.name: type-entrance-moves
cards.summary: One title-text entrance variant — letter-drop-physics (characters fall under gravity, bounce, settle at a tilt, and on the last beat all snap upright into place together)
cards.use_when: Entrances of big titles / chapter title cards; the same category as type-assembly-moves (assembly family) and document-typewriter-reveal (typewriter), chosen mutually exclusively
cards.duration: single variant 5s (including hold and a still ending; action segment ~116f, demo 150f)
cards.energy: Medium-high (physical fun)
cards.intent: The title-entrance library already has the typewriter (a steady document feel) and the assembly family (characters converging from elsewhere), and this card adds physical comedy — characters fall from the sky, slam into the ground and bounce, settle crooked and wobbly, and on the last beat all snap upright into place together, suited to ice-breaking openers with a light tone (the demo has the brand name "Shotcraft" slam down and settle, with the subtitle "Every shot lands on the beat." surfacing on the beat of the snap into place). At most 2 title-entrance variants per film (P4).

styles.label: letter-drop-physics — Letter drop
styles.description: A title text entrance style: letter-drop-physics, characters dropping (gravity slam, bounce, settling crooked, with a final beat where all straighten up and snap into place together)
styles.use: Light-toned openers; a title icebreaker with a 'living thing' feel

cards.name: type-rhythm-sync
cards.summary: Two variants of text synchronised to sound — font-weight-pump (strokes thicken on drum hits and spring back) and karaoke-fill-sync (words light up one by one with the narration)
cards.use_when: Passages where a title / tagline is strongly bound to the audio track; A binds to the beat (drum hits), B binds to speech (narration word by word)
cards.duration: A FontWeightPump 165f / B KaraokeFillSync 150f; A 128 BPM with 14f per beat and a 9–13f decay window, B each word 18–33f according to speaking rate
cards.energy: A high (club feel) / B medium (read-along guidance)
cards.intent: Everything in the text-motion library until now was about "how it enters", and nothing governed "how text already on screen comes alive with the sound". These two variants fill that gap: A turns the title into a rhythm organ — strokes twitching thicker on the bass drum and springing back, the text dancing, suited to a visual subwoofer for high-energy passages; B turns the tagline into read-along captions — whichever word the narration reads, that word fills with colour and lights up from left to right, the gaze led along, suited to voice-over / tagline emphasis passages. What they share is **the text does not move, the attributes do**: no displacement, no entrance or exit, purely weight / colour breathing on the sound's beat points.

styles.label: font-weight-pump — Weight pulse
styles.description: On the hit frame strokes instantly thicken (stroke + font-weight jump), decaying and springing back over ~10f; accented beats additionally widen by 8%
styles.use: Music-driven high-energy segments; the title as a subwoofer

styles.label: karaoke-fill-sync — Fill-along reading
styles.description: Each word fills dark from left to right, with progress following speech rate and holding once read; an underline with a reading pointer sits beneath the active word
styles.use: Narration / voice-over emphasis segments; guiding the eye through multi-word taglines

cards.name: typewriter-moves
cards.summary: Typewriter error-retype — a three-act drama of the "retraction" by mistaken delete and retype: type out a mediocre word → hesitate → backspace to delete it → type out the selling-point word faster
cards.use_when: Slogan / selling-point title cards, negation-style copy; text entrances with a built-in sense of time
cards.energy: Medium-low
cards.intent: Typing is the only text entrance with a built-in sense of time — the characters arriving one by one is itself the rhythm, and no extra motion is needed. Variant A treats typing as a **monologue**: type out a mediocre word character by character (in the demo, "just a slideshow" under the eyebrow Introducing video-shotcraft) → a pause of hesitation → backspace to delete it → type out the selling-point word faster ("your cinematic crew"), a three-act drama of hesitation-negation-declaration, with all the drama in the difference among three speeds.

styles.label: error-retype
styles.description: Typewriter error-retype: a three-act 'correcting yourself' play of deleting and retyping: types a mediocre word → hesitates → backspaces it → types the selling-point word faster
styles.use: The 'correcting yourself' beat on slogan cards; negation-style copy

cards.name: vertical-word-roll-blur-cycle
cards.summary: The word at the end of the sentence is replaced by a vertical roller, with 3 word changes of 0.55s each (70% outQuint + 30% outBack, fast first then extremely slow with a slight overshoot), adjacent rows getting vertical blur and greyscale by distance, and the centre word turning from grey to the accent colour at the instant it settles
cards.use_when: One-line selling points of the "Crafted for ___" / "Built for ___" kind, a sentence stem + a list of audiences / targets; a clean beat in a light-ground brand film
cards.duration: about 5.0s (150f@30fps: rest → 3 word changes → the whole group fades out at the tail)
cards.energy: Medium (a steady three beats, no peak)
cards.intent: The best solution for changing the word at the end of a sentence is a roller rather than a fade in and out: a roller carries a **direction** of its own (turning a page upward), and the audience knows "there is a next one". The two identity markers of this card are the **vertical blur** of adjacent rows (roller depth of field, simulating the defocus of a mechanical drum) and the **colouring** at settling (grey → accent colour, "this is the answer"). The sentence stem (demo `Crafted for`) stays absolutely still throughout — the eyes are pinned on the roller, and if the stem so much as wobbles the listing feel falls apart.

styles.label: vertical-word-roll-blur-cycle
styles.description: The word at the end of the sentence becomes a vertical wheel, with 3 word changes of 0.55s each (70% outQuint + 30% outBack, fast at first then extremely slow with a slight overshoot), adjacent rows getting vertical blur and grayscale by distance, and the center word turning from gray to the accent color the moment it settles

cards.name: word-relay-filmstrip
cards.summary: A left column of equal-height page cards alternating black and white scrolls in steps (the focus card fully lit, neighbouring cards defocused and dimmed), while a large serif word on the right relays in place (constant noun + rotating verb) — it scrolls one notch only at the instant of a word change, with the word block's vertical centre aligned exactly to the midpoint of the current page card
cards.use_when: Enumeration passages of "one subject × many capabilities" (Shotcraft frames/builds/ships…); portfolio / case-flow displays; a multi-scene tour of a product
cards.duration: each word period ~1.5–2s × 3–4 words; demo 180f (6s)
cards.energy: Medium-low (an editorial-desk temperament, with the rhythm coming from the "click" of the word change)
cards.intent: The left is evidence (a film strip of page screenshots) and the right is the argument (the big word): each time the verb changes, the strip steps one notch to give new evidence — text and picture footnoting each other. The crux is **stepping**: the left column is completely still most of the time, and scrolls one notch only at the instant of a word change (scrolling = the mechanical action of changing evidence); continuous scrolling reduces the left column to background decoration and the word change loses its "click". The second crux is **alignment**: the vertical centre of the big word block must be aligned exactly (to the pixel) to the midpoint of the current page card, and if it is off the whole layout's "editorial rigour" collapses.

styles.label: word-relay-filmstrip
styles.description: The left column of black-and-white alternating equal-height page cards scrolls in steps (focus card fully lit, neighbors defocused and dimmed) while a large serif word on the right relays in place (noun constant + verb rotating); it scrolls one notch only at the moment the word switches, with the word block's vertical center precisely aligned to the current page card's midpoint

cards.name: word-relay-geometry
cards.summary: Three benefit words each carry their own dedicated geometry relay — a dashed large circle spinning with deceleration + a comet arc running → three solid circles growing by trim in turn and then closing in to bite tight → a chrome metallic sheen sweeping past and then, a beat later, settling to pure white; the old word shrinks to 0.86 and fades out, the new word is revealed outline → fill
cards.use_when: Three-point benefit statements (faster / better / stronger); brand-values passages; a mid-section push that needs "one word, one world"
cards.duration: about 6.0s (180f@30fps: three segments of ≈60f each, with 6f overlap between segments)
cards.energy: Medium-high (a three-beat push + geometric motion throughout + background particles, no still frames)
cards.intent: A three-point benefit statement is most easily made as three title cards hard-cut together. The relay approach gives each word a set of **geometry that belongs only to it**: the dashed circle is "turning" (fast), three circles interlocking and closing in is "biting into each other" (tight / good), and the metallic sheen is "hard material" (strong) — the geometry itself is arguing in place of the adjective. The third word gets an elevated treatment (sheen sweep + settling to white) because it is the conclusion. Background dust motes, the shared stage light and the three-segment progress bar at the bottom stitch the three beats into one continuous space, otherwise it is still three cards.

styles.label: word-relay-geometry
styles.description: Three benefit words each carry their own geometric relay: a dashed large circle decelerating spin + a comet arc flying along → three solid-line circles trimming on in turn then contracting and clamping tight → a chrome-metal sheen sweeps through and a beat later settles to pure white; the old word shrinks to 0.86 and fades out, the new word reveals outline → fill

cards.name: avatar-bracket-carousel
cards.summary: "Your ___ agent" fill-in-the-blank typography; four corner focus brackets are pinned in place mid-sentence while a queue of avatars rotates vertically through the frame on a spring three times. An avatar entering the frame scales up and sharpens; leaving, it shrinks, fades and blurs by distance. The role label swaps in sync, and the brackets breathe 7% at each switch
cards.use_when: Enumerating abilities as "one slot, many roles"; the core one-line shot for team / identity / preset / persona products
cards.duration: about 5.2s (156f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium (three evenly spaced switches form a steady metronome; the bracket pulse is the only decorative motion)
cards.intent: "Our agent can be a director, an editor, an animator, a sound designer" listed as four rows is just a checklist. Fitted into one slot of a single sentence, it becomes one promise plus four proofs: the sentence stays still and only the person in the slot changes. The four corner brackets are the key to this technique - they do not take part in the rotation, but they pin the viewer's eye to that 92×92 box, so the four swaps read as "the same slot" rather than "four avatars drifting past".

styles.label: avatar-bracket-carousel
styles.description: A 'Your ___ agent' fill-in-the-blank layout with four corner focus brackets pinned in place mid-sentence; a queue of avatars rotates vertically with spring easing three times inside the brackets, scaling up and sharpening as it enters the frame and shrinking, fading and blurring by distance as it leaves; role labels swap in sync, and the brackets breathe 7% at each switch

cards.name: bezier-source-converge-merge
cards.summary: Four source nodes on the left each have a thin Bézier curve leading to the same convergence point on the right. The curves draw on from left to right in a stagger, the nodes slide along their own curves towards the convergence point and shrink in three stages with acceleration until they vanish, accent-coloured data packets glide along the paths throughout, and once the merge completes the curves are wiped back from the left end leaving only the brand mark (demo: a white porcelain disc carrying the video-shotcraft brand-mark mark)
cards.use_when: The core mechanism shot for "multi-source integration / unified access / data convergence"; explanatory segments for integration, aggregation and single-entry-point products
cards.duration: about 5.6s (168f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium (a long shot that advances slowly, kept alive by the gliding data packets; the moment of merging is the only small high point)
cards.intent: "We unified four sources" is an abstract sentence. This motion turns it into a physical process you can watch: first establish four independent pathways (draw-on reads as "connected"), then let the four sources actually walk along those pathways into the same point and be sucked in (shrinking to 0 reads as "merged"), and finally erase the pathways and leave only the brand mark ("now there is only one"). Each of the three narrative phases has a clear start and end, and viewers can read the cause and effect without narration.

styles.label: bezier-source-converge-merge
styles.description: Four source nodes on the left each connect to a single convergence point on the right via a thin Bezier curve; the curves draw on from left to right with stagger, nodes slide along their own curves toward the convergence point and shrink to nothing with a three-stage acceleration, and an accent-color data packet glides along the paths throughout; once the merge completes, the curves erase backward from the left end, leaving only the brand mark (demo: a white porcelain disc holding the video-shotcraft mark)

cards.name: card-stack
cards.summary: A set of template cards (9 in the demo) spring in one by one from below the screen, landing faster and faster into a pile; once all are in place the whole pile fans out in one go - each card turned 6.5° and shifted 138px sideways according to its index - and finally the centre card is pulled out
cards.use_when: Product segments that need to establish "we have a set of things"; establishing shots for card walls / template libraries / plan lists, and can also serve as a beat of anticipation before a logo
cards.duration: about 5.0s (150f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium-high (the entrance is a run of small bursts, and the fan-out section resolves into one smooth whole-body motion)
cards.intent: A pile of cards first gathers into one object, then spreads out into a set of objects - the order is crucial: give the "whole" first, then the "individuals". What viewers remember at first glance is a weighty pile (a sense of quantity), and only at second glance do they see that each card is different (variety). The fan-out is held back to the end and done in one go so that it does not fight with the entrance's beat.

styles.label: card-stack
styles.description: A set of template cards (9 in the demo) spring in one by one from below the screen, landing faster and faster into a pile; once all are in place, the whole pile fans out at once, each card rotated by 6.5° and shifted 138px per index, and finally the center card is pulled out

cards.name: carousel-3d
cards.summary: 8 cards are arranged in a ring and the whole ring rotates one full turn (a constant-speed base plus a stepped component that docks every 45°); each card only revolves around Y and is itself a billboard facing outwards, with two layers of same-direction texture (front and back) plus backface-visibility:hidden so it is always upright and never inverted. The card at the front is lit and the caption below the ring changes text accordingly, and the camera stays pinned at a shallow downward angle throughout
cards.use_when: Looping showcases of portfolios / template libraries / integration lists; background shots or landing page heroes that need a seamless loop
cards.duration: about 5.6s (168f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium (a steady-state motion that can loop forever, with a docking beat every 45°)
cards.intent: The easiest way to show "a set of things" is to line them up for a horizontal slide, but a horizontal slide has a start and an end. A ring does not - it naturally loops, and no matter how long the viewer watches it never feels "finished". What this card really solves is the point where a ring carousel most easily goes wrong: the back of the cards. The approach is double-sided same-direction texture, so seen from inside the ring or outside it is the same upright card, and over one full turn of the ring no frame shows a mirrored or inverted card.

styles.label: carousel-3d
styles.description: 8 cards arranged in a ring rotate as a whole through one full turn (constant-speed base plus a stepped stop every 45°); each card orbits only around Y and billboards outward, with front and back layers textured in the same direction plus backface-visibility:hidden so cards are always upright, never inverted; the card at the front lights up and the caption beneath the ring changes text accordingly, with the camera pinned at a shallow high angle throughout

cards.name: cloner-depth-echo
cards.summary: Clone column - the main card instantly "photocopies" 7 semi-transparent clones that line up in a queue along a diagonal depth axis, hold for a beat, then all accelerate back into the original, merging into one with a bounce
cards.use_when: Selling points of "multiple copies / multi-tenancy / sense of scale / batch processing"; one shot that tells "one = many"
cards.duration: 138f (about 4.6s)
cards.energy: Medium (display-then-converge type)
cards.intent: A UI translation of the Spline/C4D Cloner vocabulary: one main card "pops" out 7 clones, spaced evenly back along the Z axis (interval 250px, opacity decreasing 100%→28%, the further away the more only an outline remains), popping out in a stagger to form a column; it holds for ~32f so the viewer can count that "there are many"; then all of them ease-in, accelerating back into the original to merge, and at the moment of merging the original bounces to 1.06x to close. The demo lands "one = many" on a concrete selling point: one video-shotcraft render card (launch-film) × 8 shots; on merging, the 8 shot slots at the bottom of the card light up together, and the title lands on "One prompt. / Eight shots.". The division of labour with the depth-layer-moves parallax (different content in layers): this is an evenly spaced echo array of the **same content**, and its meaning is scale not space.

styles.label: cloner-depth-echo
styles.description: Cloner column: the main card instantly 'photocopies' 7 semi-transparent duplicates that line up in a diagonal depth column, hold for a beat, then all accelerate back into the original, merging with a bounce

cards.name: deck-deal-flyin
cards.summary: Opens with an orbiting close-up of a physical card pile on a dark graphite desktop; the light moves from the pile to the page board beside it, a stack of cards is hard-accelerated into a grid like a deal, and the camera chases the deal, rising and tilting back, to settle and hold on a runway-style overhead of the fully filled board
cards.use_when: List pages and card walls that show "large volume of content / a continuous inflow"; building a first impression of information density
cards.duration: 150f (about 5s: 0-36 pile close-up + anticipation, 36-~101 deal, 108-150 full-board hold)
cards.energy: High (the main force of the rhythm-climbing segment; do not use as the opening first shot)
cards.intent: Give the suspense first (what is this pile?), then the answer (dozens of items that fly into the page and each take their place). The viewer should feel "things pouring in without end", with every card slamming into place with urgency.

styles.label: deck-deal-flyin
styles.description: Opens with an orbiting close-up of a physical card deck on a dark graphite tabletop; the light moves from the deck to the page board beside it, a stack of cards is flung into the grid with hard acceleration like a deal, and the camera chases the deal, rising and tilting back, to freeze on a runway-style overhead of the fully loaded board

cards.name: doc-park-left-pill-deal
cards.summary: The document does not fade out but slides left, showing only about 35% of its width and shrinking slightly to 0.92; on the right, three white outlined pills are dealt slowly at the narration's pace (popping in with outBack); after each one lands, the caption beneath it deepens word by word, and the whole sentence fades before the next arrives; the document on the left auto-scrolls extremely slowly throughout to keep up the "being read" feel
cards.use_when: Narration-driven segments where "analysis conclusions are given one by one"; the core explanatory shot for document understanding, recommendation reasons and review comment products
cards.duration: about 5.8s (174f@30fps)
cards.energy: Low (slow dealing rhythm, no peaks across the film; liveliness is kept up by the auto-scroll)
cards.intent: Conclusions have to be given one at a time for viewers to remember them. But if the source document is faded out, the conclusions become castles in the air - viewers do not know where these words come from. This card's solution is to **keep the source in the frame**: the document stays parked on the left showing only a strip, still scrolling slowly (showing it is being read), and each conclusion on the right grows out of this document. The dealing rhythm is deliberately slow, to leave the narration time to finish a sentence.

styles.label: doc-park-left-pill-deal
styles.description: The document does not fade out but slides left until only about 35% of its width shows and shrinks slightly to 0.92; on the right, three white outlined pills are dealt slowly to the narration rhythm (outBack spring-in), the subtitle beneath each one deepens word by word after it lands and fades out as a whole line before the next arrives, while the left document auto-scrolls very slowly throughout to stay 'being read'

cards.name: draw-svg-trace
cards.summary: Stroke-growth circling - a line of ink with a pen tip runs once around an element's outline to "draw" it; at the instant it closes, a black flash hands over and the content fades in; the same routine can underline a title
cards.use_when: The called-out entrance of a single card / chart / title; an element-level technique (the page-level blueprint line trace belongs to wall-reveal-moves style B)
cards.duration: 132f (teaser 10f + stroke 40f + black-flash handover 16f + underline 18f + hold 40f, about 4.4s)
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intent: "Drawn out" is the most natural entrance metaphor in the paper-and-ink aesthetic: the element does not fly in or fade in, but is traced on the spot by an invisible pen. The library's wall-reveal-moves style B already has a whole-page blueprint version (a full-screen wireframe drawn segment by segment + areas lit up); this card is its **element-level close-up**: one line, one subject, one closure, with the pen tip visible and the direction readable, suited to the "next we talk about it" moment of calling something out. The second use is a growing title underline: the same routine in an 18f short version, giving a key word a single hand-drawn stroke of emphasis, naturally in the same family as the marker aesthetic token.

styles.label: draw-svg-trace
styles.description: Stroke-growth callout: an ink line with a pen tip runs once around an element's outline to 'draw' it; at the moment it closes it flashes black as a handoff and the content fades in; the same technique can draw an underline beneath a title

cards.name: element-body-moves
cards.summary: Element body feel - contact-shadow-lift (the contact shadow lifts off the surface): as a card lifts, the shadow on the table enlarges and fades in sync, and the paper leaving the table is proved by its shadow
cards.use_when: Supplementing "position changes" with "body changes": gives a called-out card evidence of hovering; pairs with 2.5D camera moves and card-by-card call-outs
cards.duration: A 150f 5s
cards.energy: A low-medium
cards.intent: All the motion cards in the library handle "position changes" - flying in, sliding, bouncing - and the element itself always stays a rigid body. This style handles **body changes**: it gives hovering a believable piece of evidence - as the card lifts, the shadow directly beneath it enlarges and fades in sync, the paper leaves the table, and the staging principle lays down the physical lines for the 2.5D camera moves. The difference from CameraMotionBlur: shutter trails are the camera's business, while lifting off the surface is the body's business.

styles.label: contact-shadow-lift
styles.description: Element body feel: contact-shadow-lift, where a card lifts off the surface while its shadow on the table scales up and fades in sync, the shadow proving the paper has left the desk
styles.use: Calling out cards one by one for emphasis; off-surface setup for 2.5D sections

cards.name: integration-hub-map
cards.summary: The old page flips 180° in one fast turn (the side edge flashes brightly for an instant) and lands as the new hub page; five integration app icons pop in on the same frame, then five rainbow light tubes connect together on the same frame, and conveying pulses inside the tubes keep flowing - "turn to a new page, and the whole ecosystem plugs in at once"
cards.use_when: Integration / ecosystem capability segments (one product connects to everything); version-refresh narratives (old page turns into new page); the feature climax in a dark-scene neon tone
cards.duration: wind-up ~0.5s + fast flip ~1.2s + icons appear together → tubes connect together, two beats ~0.7s + conveying breathing ≥1.5s; whole segment 4.5-5s
cards.energy: Medium-high (the flip is the burst, the conveying segment is the afterglow)
cards.intent: The flip is "changing eras": the old document page flips a full 180° to become the new hub page - it must be a complete flip and not just turning through some angle (precedent), and the flip action is a **fast flip + decelerating tail**, completed in one go with no pauses in between (the "constant speed" precedent: what the user meant by constant speed is no pausing, not literal linear; the version with a pause at the 90° side edge was rejected). At the side-edge moment it only "flashes once" (a 1-3f pulse; a long glow plateau was rejected). The connection is a **two-beat system**: five icons pop in on the same frame (beat one) → the five tubes start drawing on the same frame and connect together (beat two) - being together is what reads as "the ecosystem arrives in one go"; connecting one by one in a stagger reads as negotiating one by one (rejected in two rounds). After connection, bright pulses inside the tubes circulate continuously in the icon → hub direction, and the "feeling of conveying" is the life of the end state.

styles.label: integration-hub-map
styles.description: The old page flips 180° in one fast snap (edges flash bright instantly) to land as the new hub page, five integration app icons pop in on the same frame, then five rainbow light tubes all connect on the same frame, with pulses flowing continuously inside the tubes; 'turn a new page, the ecosystem plugs in all at once'

cards.name: list-reveal
cards.summary: Six items of a vertical menu find their place one after another at 10f intervals by scale, settling with a soft back slight overshoot, while the whole list container moves up at constant speed throughout - item-by-item entrance and overall drift are two unrelated layers of motion
cards.use_when: Entrances of navigation / sidebar / settings panels; any UI segment where "the interface grows itself", and also suitable as a low-energy bed while narration sets things up
cards.duration: about 4s (120f@30fps)
cards.energy: Low (steady beat, no peaks; the drift keeps the picture from dying)
cards.intent: A list fading in item by item is the kind of motion most easily made stiff: each item stops once it has moved, and the picture is completely still between two items. This card's solution is to add a layer of slow drift to the container, unrelated to the item-by-item entrance - locally the items are "finding their place", and globally the whole is "breathing". Viewers can read every item, and yet not a single frame of the picture is nailed down from start to finish.

styles.label: list-reveal
styles.description: 6 items of a vertical menu scale into position one after another at 10f intervals with a soft back easing and slight overshoot, while the whole list container moves up at constant speed throughout; per-item entrance and overall drift are two unrelated layers of motion

cards.name: list-stack-press
cards.summary: List cards fly up from the bottom of the frame one by one and pile up; each landing presses and bounces the whole pile, and the counter jumps one notch in sync
cards.use_when: Feed / radar / inbox shots about "something new every day"; asset lists that emphasise continuous accumulation
cards.duration: about 3s (18-88f)
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intent: "A pile has weight": as each new card lands, the whole pile of already-settled cards is pressed down and bounces back - viewers read from the physical feedback that "this is something really accumulated". The counter jumping a notch in sync nails down the sense of quantity.

styles.label: list-stack-press
styles.description: List cards fly up one by one from the bottom of the frame and pile up, each landing presses and bounces the whole stack while a counter ticks up one notch in sync

cards.name: neon-frame-forerun
cards.summary: A strongly perspective right-angled neon frame races on from both ends of the left edge and takes shape first; the page goes from dark to lit inside the frame while the components/text inside drop in from above in 3D with same-shape soft shadows, staggered, completing their fit in sync as the page lights up; the background neon group (in the demo, a depth-echo tunnel of same-shaped frames) goes out in the final segment to give way
cards.use_when: In a dark-scene brand film, giving a UI panel an "appearance ceremony" (frame first, content after); the first reveal of a feature area; segment openers in a neon / cyber tone
cards.duration: frame race ~0.7s + light-up & drop-in ~2.7s + background-off wrap-up ~1s; whole segment 4-4.7s (demo 140f)
cards.energy: Medium-high (three layers of action stack in, but all serve the same appearance)
cards.intent: Set the frame first, then fill in the flesh: the neon wireframe races from both ends like runway lights to outline the position, announcing "something is about to appear here"; while the page goes from dark to lit inside the frame, the components drop in from the air with their shadows - viewers see the interface being "placed" into the frame. The three layers of action (frame race / page light-up / component drop-in) must **mesh in sync**: the drop-in progress advances in step with the light-up progress and finishes slightly behind it, and the frame light finally merges into the panel glow. The background neon tube group goes out in the final segment, yielding brightness to the protagonist to complete the wrap-up.

styles.label: neon-frame-forerun
styles.description: A strong-perspective right-angle neon frame draws from both ends of the left edge to take shape ahead of the page, and the page inside the frame goes from dark to light; at the same time the components/text inside the frame drop in from above in 3D with matching soft shadows, staggered, completing their landing in sync with the page lighting up, and the background neon cluster (in the demo, a depth echo tunnel of same-shape frames) goes out in the final segment to make way

cards.name: neon-frame-orbit-drop
cards.summary: After the neon frame draws first, the camera arcs around the page from left to right, and all the page's components/text drop from the air and fit down on the **same frame** (same-shape soft shadows converging in sync) - an all-at-once, placed-in-the-frame appearance
cards.use_when: A one-time grand entrance of a single UI page (as opposed to a tour / area-by-area reveal); the main-visual unveiling of a dark-scene neon-tone segment; the sister shot of neon-frame-forerun
cards.duration: frame draw ~0.5s + rotation & simultaneous drop-in ~2.5s + settle ~1s; whole segment ~4.7s (140f, rotation ends at 128f and then leaves the settle)
cards.energy: Medium-high (a one-time big action that goes still once settled)
cards.intent: The twin variant of neon-frame-forerun: likewise frame first, content after, but the camera is not fixed - it rotates in a continuous arc from a viewpoint on the left of the page to one on the right, and while the rotation is under way all the components drop from the air. The crux is **simultaneous fit**: all components and text lift, fall and fit on the same frame, and the soft shadows vanish in sync - this is the grammar of "an all-at-once appearance" (precedent: the staggered version was rejected as "it should be all components and text dropping from the air and fitting down at the same time"). A staggered drop-in belongs to the tour shot (graze-face-tour); a single page's one-time reveal must drop together, and the rhythm semantics must not be mixed.

styles.label: neon-frame-orbit-drop
styles.description: After the neon frame draws ahead, the camera rotates around the page on a left-to-right arc while all the page's components/text drop from the air and settle on the **same frame** (matching soft shadows converging in sync); an all-at-once entrance placement inside the frame

cards.name: page-waterfall-wall
cards.summary: Page waterfall wall - real page screenshots cut into 3-4 columns scroll endlessly in opposite directions at different speeds on a 3D reclined wall surface, with parallax + a slow camera push giving an overview of "so much content it never finishes flowing"
cards.use_when: Segments about the volume of "many pages / many features / many templates"; the spread in the middle of a montage or a product-breadth shot after the intro
cards.duration: 4-6s (an infinite loop body; the duration is cut to what the segment needs)
cards.energy: Medium (flowing display type)
cards.intent: A flowing overview: let the viewer "see many pages flow past" within a few seconds, with the read being volume rather than detail. Division of labour with outro-group-photo-launch: that is a **gathering** overview (elements fly in to surround the wordmark and freeze into a group photo, with the meaning "belongs to the same product"), while this card is a **flowing** overview (content flows past continuously without freezing, with the meaning "there is still a lot we have not shown you"). Division of labour with wall-reveal-moves: that is the whole wall's **entrance action**, while this card is the wall's **ongoing state**, and that card's entrance can hand over to this card to carry on flowing.

styles.label: page-waterfall-wall
styles.description: Page waterfall wall: real page screenshots are cut into 3-4 columns and scroll endlessly in opposite directions at different speeds on a 3D reclined wall, with parallax + a slow camera push-in making an overview of 'so much content it never stops flowing'

cards.name: product-card-progressive-assemble
cards.summary: A detail card builds itself as if its fields were being scraped one by one - a "fill cursor" leaps ahead from box to box, with image → title → category pill popping in turn → the original price appears and is then struck through and demoted, the accent-colour new price springing out → the body text is revealed line by line with a highlight block sweeping from left to right → the swatches light up → the button fills; the whole card pushes forward with a very slow scale throughout
cards.use_when: Capability showcases of product / entry detail pages; the main shot of "structured extraction", "auto-fill" and "data grows by itself" narratives
cards.duration: about 5.7s (172f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium (small events densely laid out in succession, no single-point burst; the forward push keeps the sense of progress)
cards.intent: If a detail card simply fades in, the viewer only sees "there is a card". Placing it field by field turns the card into a **form being filled in**: each field arrives on its own, and the viewer's attention is led once through the card's information structure - where the image is, where the title is, where the price is, where the body's key points are. The price strike-through demotion is the only semantic event in the whole film (not "appearing" but "changing"), so it is scheduled in the most prominent position in the middle.

styles.label: product-card-progressive-assemble
styles.description: A detail card builds itself as if being scraped field by field: a 'fill cursor' jumps ahead from cell to cell, image → title → category pill pop in one after another → the original price appears and is then struck through and demoted while the accent-color new price springs out → body text reveals line by line with a highlight block brushing left to right → color swatches light up → the button fills; the whole card pushes forward at a very slow scale throughout

cards.name: radial-wave
cards.summary: A 17×9 array of dots lights up in a stagger by Euclidean distance from the wave source; each dot's scale overshoots to 1.5 and then settles back to stay lit, and after the first wave has swept through, a second bright-blue pulse closes in from the outer ring back to the centre in reverse
cards.use_when: The "system powers up" beat of a product / brand opening; also used as an establishing shot for data grids, node maps and coverage-range narratives
cards.duration: about 3.8s (114f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium-high (one burst at the start, then after the wave front passes it turns into a low-energy always-lit bed)
cards.intent: It rewrites the static fact that "many dots exist at the same time" into the dynamic fact that "energy spreads from one source to the whole". What the viewer sees is not a dot matrix picture but one power-up: the centre lights first, the brightness pushes outward like a water wave, and once it has finished the whole array stays in the always-lit state - laying the ground for the content to be shown on the next beat. The second reverse wave is an acknowledgement, telling the viewer that this system responds.

styles.label: radial-wave
styles.description: A 17×9 dot array lights up with stagger by Euclidean distance to the wave source, each dot scale-overshooting to 1.5 then settling back to steady lit; after the first wave finishes sweeping, a second bright-blue pulse converges back to center from the outer ring in reverse

cards.name: research-card-stack-scroll
cards.summary: Dark paper cards fly in one every 12 frames along a lower-right axis and pile up in the centre, landing with a 1-frame compression; only the topmost card is fully rendered sharp with title + authors + abstract, while the cards beneath blur and darken with increasing pile depth and show only a title strip, and the background horizontal grid moves down in sync as a speed reference
cards.use_when: Conveying the magnitude of "read a huge amount of material / processed a vast number of documents"; capability shots for research, retrieval and batch-processing products
cards.duration: about 4.8s (144f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium-high (constant high frequency, no bursts but sustained pressure)
cards.intent: What is to be said is "quantity", but giving 13 cards at once would read as a wall. Turn it into an assembly line: cards enter one at a time, each one is read (the topmost one is always the one rendered in full text), and once read it sinks into the pile and blurs. What the viewer feels is a continuous throughput, not a static pile. The background grid moving down at the same speed is the speed reference - without it, the piling would read as "cards shrinking in place".

styles.label: research-card-stack-scroll
styles.description: Dark paper cards fly into the center one every 12 frames along a lower-right axis and stack up, landing with 1 frame of compression; only the top card is rendered fully sharp with title + authors + abstract, while cards below get progressively blurrier and darker with stack depth, showing only a title strip, and the background horizontal grid moves down in sync as a speed reference

cards.name: row-embed
cards.summary: Content rows descend from the air like cards, flatten out via rotateX, and at the instant of embedding a seam of accent colour lights up on the bottom edge
cards.use_when: Detail-page / list shots of "structured data growing into the page"; batch entrances of row-level content
cards.duration: about 2s (12-68f)
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intent: The rows of a detail page are not "displayed" but "grown into" - each row descends from the air and embeds flush into the page layout, and the accent-colour seam at the instant of embedding is the visual foley of a "click" snapping shut.

styles.label: row-embed
styles.description: A content row descends from the air like a card, flattens via rotateX, and at the moment of embedding a seam in the accent color lights along its bottom edge

cards.name: value-stagger-gradient
cards.summary: As 16 bars enter, the delay is a time stagger, while four properties - height / hue / displacement / blur - are each spread into a numeric gradient from first to last; on the second beat the stagger origin is swapped to the centre and the pulse amplitude is spread afresh with the centre as the maximum
cards.use_when: Showcase shots for technique demos and parametric capabilities; can also serve directly as the entrance of data / spectrum / equaliser-type interfaces
cards.duration: about 5.0s (150f@30fps)
cards.energy: Medium-high (the first beat is a continuous spread, the second beat's centre pulse is a definite single peak)
cards.intent: Stagger is usually used only to offset time. What this card wants to say is that it can also offset **values** - the same index decides both "when to move" and "how much to move". The two beats are a controlled experiment: in the first beat the origin is at the first position (the gradient spreads monotonically from left to right), and in the second the origin is moved to the centre (the gradient spreads symmetrically about the central axis). What the viewer sees is not two animations, but the same recipe with one parameter changed. The code caption on screen switches in sync to the corresponding stagger call, stating this outright.

styles.label: value-stagger-gradient
styles.description: As 16 bars enter, delay is the time stagger, while height/hue/offset/blur are each spread as a value gradient from first to last; on the second beat the stagger origin is switched to the center and the pulse amplitude is respread with the center as maximum

cards.name: wall-reveal-moves
cards.summary: Two styles of whole-wall batch entrance - bento lighting up cell by cell, and blueprint line tracing taking shape, all revealing in place with no displacement, complementing deck-deal-flyin's fly-in displacement type to form a category matrix
cards.use_when: The overall debut of feature walls / card walls / full-page interfaces; segments where the content is already in place and is to be "revealed" rather than "poured in"
cards.duration: about 5s per style (A 150f / B 150f @30fps, including the establishing hold and still ending)
cards.energy: Medium
cards.intent: For "how does a wall of content make its entrance" the library previously had only one answer, deck-deal-flyin - high energy, displacement type, "things pouring in". But not every wall should pour in: a brand segment needs gravity, and "from design to the real thing" needs to tell the process. What these two styles have in common is a **non-displacement batch entrance** - elements reveal in place, the layout holds from the first frame, and what the viewer watches is "a wavefront of state change sweeping across a wall" rather than "objects flying". When choosing, first ask: should this wall "pour in" or "light up"? For the former go to deck-deal-flyin, for the latter come into this card.

styles.label: bento-light-up — Cell-by-cell light-up
styles.description: A dark-field 3×2 bento wall stands dimmed by, an amber light stream traces each cell's outline one by one around once, after which the content brightens and floats up, and once all are lit the camera slowly pushes in to settle
styles.use: Solemn content / dark-field brand segments; steady-paced feature overviews

styles.label: wireframe-draw-on — Blueprint line-draw build
styles.description: The interface is first drawn group by group as an SVG thin-line blueprint, then a glowing amber vertical line sweeps left to right, and the wireframe solidifies into the real interface where it passes
styles.use: 'From design to reality / from idea to product' narratives; a product's first full reveal
